s1.name: The Midnight Hunger
s1.plot: Something in the village is eating well after dark.

s2.name: The Dark Forest Law
s2.plot: A new law sends everyone through the woods at night.

s3.name: The Villafish Feast
s3.plot: The fishing contest ends with more than fish missing.

s4.name: The Full Moon Festival
s4.plot: The festival dances on while two villagers vanish.

s5.name: The Christmas Secret
s5.plot: Odd bite marks appear under the tree on Christmas night.

s6.name: The Haunted Mill
s6.plot: Everyone blames the mill spirits. Something else is hunting.

s7.name: The Frozen Lake Mystery
s7.plot: Footprints cross the frozen lake and stop halfway.

s8.name: The Lost Eye Legend
s8.plot: A tale about a lost eye hides something darker.

s9.name: The Golden Season
s9.plot: The season comes in rich. The village grows thin.

s10.name: The Silent Village
s10.plot: By midnight nobody is left awake to scream.

s11.name: The Old Castle
s11.plot: Repairs on the old castle uncover tunnels nobody dug.

s12.name: The River Howl
s12.plot: Howls rise from the river every single night.

s13.name: The Broken Bell
s13.plot: The bell rings at midnight. Nobody admits ringing it.

s14.name: The Shadow Market
s14.plot: An after-dark market. Best not ask what's for sale.

s15.name: The Moonlight Race
s15.plot: A midnight race through the woods. Not everyone finishes.

s16.name: The Forgotten Mine
s16.plot: Tools lie abandoned deep in the old mine.

s17.name: The Candle Mystery
s17.plot: A candle burns in one window nightly. It's a signal.

s18.name: The Rainy Night
s18.plot: The storm washed away everything except the footprints.

s19.name: The Secret Garden
s19.plot: A hidden garden takes visitors long after midnight.

s20.name: The Wolf Mask Party
s20.plot: Everyone wears a wolf mask. Two aren't pretending.

s21.name: The Missing Lanterns
s21.plot: The lanterns keep vanishing and the streets go dark.

s22.name: The Midnight Market
s22.plot: Secrets are traded at a market nobody admits to running.

s23.name: The Stormy Night
s23.plot: Thunder covered the screams. The mud kept the tracks.

s24.name: The Hidden Door
s24.plot: A door nobody remembers building stands open.

s25.name: The Village Anniversary
s25.plot: The celebration is starting to feel like a trap.

s26.name: The Broken Boat
s26.plot: A wrecked boat drifts ashore packed with clues.

s27.name: The Crimson Stain
s27.plot: The stain on the doorstep will not wash away.

s28.name: The Hollow House
s28.plot: The empty house is lit from inside every night.

s29.name: The Whispering Woods
s29.plot: The woods whisper, and villagers keep walking in.

s30.name: The Silver Moon
s30.plot: Under a silver moon, two villagers change.

s31.name: The Forgotten Feast
s31.plot: A feast is laid out. Nobody remembers cooking it.

s32.name: The Village Tournament
s32.plot: The tournament crowns a champion and loses a villager.

s33.name: The Old Lighthouse
s33.plot: The lighthouse beam swings inland on the worst nights.

s34.name: The Secret Recipe
s34.plot: A guarded recipe calls for one unusual ingredient.

s35.name: The Secret Order
s35.plot: Something is being made in secret. Nobody will say what.

s36.name: The River Festival
s36.plot: Paper boats drift downriver. One returns bloodied.

s37.name: The Long Night
s37.plot: The longest night of the year, and nobody sleeps.

s38.name: The Locked Tower
s38.plot: The tower is locked from the inside.

s39.name: The Winter Village
s39.plot: Snow covers the village and preserves every track.

s40.name: The Midnight Train
s40.plot: The midnight train arrives one passenger short.

s41.name: The Lost Treasure
s41.plot: The treasure turned up. So did the bodies.

s42.name: The Empty Rooms
s42.plot: Rooms keep emptying overnight. Nobody checks out.

s43.name: The Crystal Cave
s43.plot: Deep in the cave, the crystals are streaked red.

s44.name: The Red Moon Night
s44.plot: The moon runs red and the village bolts its doors.

s45.name: The Village Circus
s45.plot: The circus came to town. So did the attacks.

s46.name: The Secret Tunnel
s46.plot: A tunnel runs beneath the village. Someone uses it.

s47.name: The Golden Crown
s47.plot: The crown changes hands. A villager disappears.

s48.name: The Final Festival
s48.plot: The year's last festival. It may be someone's last.

s49.name: The Last Midnight
s49.plot: One more midnight before the village runs out of time.

s50.name: The Cursed Well
s50.plot: The well is cursed, they say. The water disagrees.

baker.text: Yesterday evening at 8PM I was just kneading my dough! I was there all night, kneading away.
Lalala. I made a LOVELY batch of bread last night.
I knew it wasn't the fisherman, he is the least fishy guy I know! Last night I baked a fresh aromatic batch of dough.
Another bitingly good load of bread baked last night!
I always knew that fisherman was fishy!
I have a new idea for a recipe. Sourdough a la villager!

fisherman.text: I went to the Blue Moon Inn at 8PM to get an ale with the butcher!
I went to the Blue Moon Inn Last night, and bumped into the mayor. He looked very succulent, I mean sad!
The Butcher and I had a cool ale in the Blue Moon Inn.
Shame about the barmaid. The Butcher and I decided to go fishing anyway last night.
My darling friend the butcher is gone! I wondered why he didn't show up to the Blue Moon Inn last night.
Last night I was fishing for villagers... Ahem, I mean salmon!
Only a few more villagers I can use as bait... Oh, did I say that out loud?

barmaid.text: I had to go home early from work, to handle some business...
All these deaths are getting out of hand. I was in the Blue Moon all night. It was totally empty!
You sent my lov... Business partner to jail! I was in the Blue Moon all night. It was totally empty!
I can't believe it! My lov... I mean business contact is DEAD! After the WONDERFUL chat we had last night. Unbelievable.
I am totally bored of this now. This werewolf is giving... cringe.
Only 3 of us left? And one is a werewolf? AWKWARD!

mayor.text: The barmaid and I were discussing very important and confidential information. All night!
I had a very pleasant meeting with the Barmaid. The Blue Moon inn was totally empty!
My Darling barmaid... WHY OH WHY??? I need to get a sword from the blacksmith!
My lov... Business partner was in jail. So we couldn't discuss business! I was having a late night stroll.
This is getting a bit ridiculous now. My approval rating is going down!
Only 2 of my trusty voters left? How on earth will I get a majority now.

farmer.text: I went to the Bakers house around 8PM. My horses love his bread! He didn't answer the door though...
I missed all the commotion last night. I watched water at the fishing spot. I saw someone in the distance, but couldn't make them out.
I went to the bakery last night, I forgot you put the baker in jail! On my walk back I did hear lots of giggling in the Blue Moon Inn.
I missed all the commotion last night. I watched water at the fishing spot. I saw someone in the distance, but couldn't make them out.
I missed all the commotion last night. I watched water at the fishing spot. I saw someone in the distance, but couldn't make them out.
I missed all the commotion last night. I watched water at the fishing spot. I saw someone in the distance, but couldn't make them out.
I missed all the commotion last night. I watched water at the fishing spot. I saw someone in the distance, but couldn't make them out.
Last night I saw a wolf like creature running around with a chef hat on. Probably the chickens playing pranks again.
Last night I saw a wolf like creature running around with fishing boots on. Probably the chickens playing pranks again.
Last night I had a beautiful dream about the perfect carrot.
Last night I had a beautiful dream about the perfect carrot.

butcher.text: I went to bed very early last night. The Meat Life isn't an easy life.
I watched water at the fishing spot. I saw someone in the distance, but couldn't make them out.
I had a nice discussion with the mayor last night.
I had a nice discussion with the mayor last night. I can't believe he's gone now!
The baker came to my store last night asking if I would buy some very fresh meat. It was rather peculiar.
The fisherman came to my store last night asking if I would buy some very fresh meat. It was rather peculiar.
All the meat was stolen last night from my counter. Someone must've been hungry!
These werewolves have eaten all my produce!

beggar.text: I was laying on the street outside the mayors house. He abruptly closed his curtains, and I heard lots of strange noises!
The bakery still wasn't smelling good! So I slept at the fishing spot. I think I saw someone in the distance.
I was marauding around the bakery last night. I kept stepping in wolf shaped footprints!
I was marauding around the dock last night. I kept stepping in wolf shaped footprints!
I noticed a very large hairball on the street last night!
It's hard to sleep at night with all this howling!

blacksmith.text: I went to the butchers but he didn't answer! On the way home I saw the beggar snooping around as per usual.
I went to the bakery, but it was closed!
I was busy smithing a brilliant SWORD for the mayor! Something about protecting the village.
The butcher is GONE! Oh well, swings and roundabouts!
I went out for dinner with the baker last night. He had a ferocious appetite!
I went out for dinner with the fisherman last night. He had a ferocious appetite!
I heard a loud howl very late last night.
So... One of us is a werewolf? This could be a problem.

mayor.text: Last night I was extremely busy writing some new laws for our village!
I was telling the butcher about our new law. Mandatory late night runs in the deep dark woods!
I was at the blue moon inn gloriously presenting our new law. Mandatory late night runs in the deep dark woods!
I was going for a gallop in the deep dark woods last night.
Werewolf? I am just happy about our new jogging laws. Delicious!

butcher.text: I was at home munching the bakers bright red bread! A new recipe apparently.
The mayor had a chat about his tasty new law at the Blue Moon inn.
The mayor was a werewolf? Well I for one LOVED his late night running law!
I wish that baker would be quiet and go for a nice run in the deep dark woods!
The baker being gone doesn't dissapoint me. I hated that bread. It had no meatiness to it!
I was looking for inspiration last night in the deep dark woods. So much fresh meat! Yum.

barmaid.text: I was just working last night in the Blue Moon. The baker came in with a red loaf of bread! TBH it was mid.
I was working at the Blue Moon. I remember the butcher and mayor were having a very long conversation!
I was working again. The butcher was very sad about the mayor being a werewolf.
The blue moon was super busy last night. Weirdly, the mayor drunk a gallon of milk!
Why is the baker locked up! Now I don't have any dinner.
I can't believe the baker became dinner for a werewolf... Now I don't have any dinner! Life is totally random sometimes!
I am still trying to figure out this red bread the baker gave me... He needs to touch grass!
I was busy last night in our kitchen, cooking up this sus meat the butcher gave me.
Now the butcher and the baker are gone. I have NO IDEA where to get my food from! It's totally messing up my keto.
I can't believe this is still happening. Major bombastic side eye right now.

baker.text: Well of course I was up in the early hours. Baking a feast of haute cuisine! Bread au Rouge. Voila!
Well, at least the beggar is still around. He has my secret red ingredient!
Disaster! The beggar was the supplier of my secret red ingredient.
Such a shame the barmaid was eaten. She definitely loved my bread au Rouge!
Such a shame the barmaid is locked up. She definitely loved my bread au Rouge!
What a surprise, the mayor was a werewolf. Well, he wasn't fond of my bread anyway!
What a surprise, the butcher was a werewolf. Well, he wasn't fond of my bread anyway!
Running out of people to try my bread now. Grr!

farmer.text: I've been busy replanting my beetroots! They keep getting stolen!
I was out in the woods last night getting some more beetroot seeds. I saw a silhouette of the mayor.
I went to the Blue Moon inn last night to celebrate my beetroots growing back!
I was busy last night planting new beetroot seeds. I just don't know where my beetroots keep going!
Last night I had a beautiful dream about the perfect carrot.

beggar.text: Shh... Don't tell a soul. I've been taking the farmers beetroots and selling them to the baker!
I made a pretty penny selling beetroot juice to the baker last night!
I sat by the edge of the dark forest crunching on beetroots! I saw the butcher emerge with ripped clothes!
I nabbed more of the farmers beetroots. He will run out soon!
Another day, another FORTUNE made from selling beetroot juice.
I snuck into the bakers last night to get some bread. I found a note saying the butcher was no good!
The farmers beetroots have ran out! I hope The Baker won't be disappointed.
Welp, I think this all has something to do with that deep dark forest!

fisherman.text: I was getting ready for a nice evening run in the deep dark forest! The mayor was raving about it!
I had a lovely run last night in the deep dark woods. There was even a soothing howl in the background.
On my jog I saw the beggar sneaking into the bakers! Very suspicious.
I saw the beggar covered in red last night! Awfully suspicious given the recent happenings.
I don't know why there is such raucus in the village! I beat my personal jogging record last night.
I think I'll stay in my boat tonight instead of jogging!

blacksmith.text: I've been partaking in the bakers strangely red new bread.
I stayed at a home as a protest to the mayors new law!
For some reason the butcher keeps talking about the new law that wretched mayor wanted!
Another relaxing night for me at home. I'll have a cup of tea and wait for this to all blow over.
Well. I think I was right about not going on those runs!

fisherman.text: What an awful time of the year for this to happen. This week is the fishing competition!
Despite the accident... Fishing spirits were high. Even the barmaid was watching... Intently!
I knew that beggar was a werewolf. Always licking his lips at the fish... And me!
The second the barmaid said she did not like fishing - I knew she was a werewolf!
I was looking at our fishing catches last night. I saw the barmaid licking her lips in the distance!
Last night I was trying to find the fish we caught! I bet the pesky beggar took them!
The barmaid keeps saying: Mmm delicious fisherman. It's really putting me off my game!
The fishing competition is ruined! Atleast... I am a winner by technicality.

butcher.text: Last night I was reading the latin fish encyclopedia. Should help with the competition!
I was preparing the wonderous seabass I caught last night! Or in Latin: Dicentrarchus labrax.
I was at the Blue Moon in last night. I wanted to share my delicious Dicentrarchus labrax. But the Barmaid ate it ALL!
I was walking down the street last night. The beggar ambushed me and took my Dicentrarchus labrax!
I think I will avoid fish in the future. It's bringing nothing but bad luck.

barmaid.text: Last night I was in the Blue Moon! Everyone was talking about fishing. Like... Who cares?
Now I think about it... I really like fish... Like... REALLY! Mmmmmmm.....
Mmm... Tasty fisherman... I mean FISH! Ahem. Did something happen last night?
Hashtag Delicious Villager. At McDonalds. At Pizza Hut. So fresh!

baker.text: This fishing competition doesn't interest me. Ooh! Look at me! I'm a smelly fisherman.
I was getting some wheat from the farmer last night.
Haha! Try doing a fishing competition from prison. Fisher boy!
Oh what a SHAME the fisherman was eaten! I'm sooooo sad!
My bread recipe must be wrong. The beggar won't touch it!
I went to deliver my bread to the Blue Moon inn. But the barmaid didn't want it!
The beggar very kindly asked me for some bread. He wants it at the strike of midnight. What a great guy!
Great news! Last night the barmaid assured me she would LOVE some bread delivered at midnight to her! Hurrah!

farmer.text: I saw the baker sulking. I think he's jealous of the fisherman.
The baker came along to begrudgingly buy some wheat. He said sales have been worse recently.
I met up with the baker. He seemed very happy about the fisherman being locked up!
I met up with the baker last night. He seemed very happy about the fishermans demise!
I found a totally destroyed pair of ladies shoes in my cabbage plot yesterday.
I was bringing in my crops the other day. Usually I give something to the beggar. But he wasn't there
I prayed to the lord of the carrots last night. Saaaave me from these werewolves!

beggar.text: I was hanging around the fishing spot all night. I can't wait! I am hungry for fish.
I had a very satisfying night last night! So much tasty villa....Fish. Yes Yes! Nothing better than a villafish!
I can't believe the fishing competition is over! I loved eating the fisherman! I mean FISH!
I was talking to the barmaid last night! We both have absolutely no idea what is going on! Really!
To be honest - I am so full of tasty food. I might stop begging!
I miss howling with the barmaid! Woe is me!

mayor.text: Yes... A real disaster last night. Now this fishing competition is distracting everyone!
Aslong as the fisherman is around... We will never find that werewolf!
Well, the fisherman is gone. Atleast we can focus on that pesky werewolf now!
I simply could not sleep last night. The beggar was singing She Wolf by Shakira, by my window!
I went to the Blue Moon inn last night. I climbed through the window because it wasn't open!
I am sure the werewolves spared me, because I am the mighty mayor!

blacksmith.text: I was up all night making new fishing rods for the fishing competition this week.
Well, now with the villagers getting eaten. I can win the fishing competition easily! Booyah!
The fisherman is locked up! Maybe I can make an axe to cut the prison bars!
Shame about the fisherman. No more fishing rods needed I guess!
I stayed in last night. I am making anti-werewolf armour!
Any moment now... If I see a werewolf, it aint gonna be pretty!

fisherman.text: The village is buzzing with the upcoming full moon festival. But with these strange happenings, I've been sticking close to the lake all night.
Festival preparations are in full swing, but everyone's behaving oddly. I saw shadows near the inn and the forge last night.
The blacksmith's constant hammering at odd hours sounded too much like beastly growls. I suspected him from the start!
I always thought the barmaid was suspicious, the way she poured drinks with that hungry look in her eyes. Knew she was a werewolf all along!
Last night while checking my nets, I spotted the barmaid wandering near the woods, her eyes reflecting the moonlight strangely.
I heard unusual clanging from the forge at midnight, as if the blacksmith was forging something sinister.
The barmaid has been muttering about 'thirsty for more than ale' during the festival. It's making me uneasy!
With so much chaos, at least the festival is wrapping up. Glad I've stayed out of trouble by the water.

butcher.text: I was preparing roasts for the full moon festival feast. Spent the night sharpening my tools for the best cuts.
Last evening, I was handling some prime selections in my shop. Nothing out of the ordinary for festival prep.
The blacksmith dropped off some sharpened knives last night. He seemed unusually eager for the festival meats.
I was out late sourcing additional supplies for the feast. Can't run short during the celebrations.
These disturbances are terrible for business, but perhaps it means more portions for those who remain.

barmaid.text: I was tending the Blue Moon Inn, serving up specials for the full moon festival. Busy night with villagers toasting the moon.
Had a fantastic evening at the inn. So many thirsty patrons... for drinks, of course.
Unbelievable that the blacksmith is gone. We had such productive chats about festival setups last night.
Coordinated with the blacksmith on some late-night deliveries. We both enjoy the thrill of the festival nights!
Feeling quite satisfied after all this festival excitement. Might not need another round for a while. Ahem.
I miss those midnight prowls with the blacksmith. Such delicious adventures... I mean, discussions!

baker.text: Last night I was baking moon-shaped pastries for the festival. I was up all night perfecting the recipe.
I delivered fresh pastries to the inn last night. The barmaid seemed ravenously hungry.
Barmaid in jail? Who will sample my festival treats now?
The barmaid gone? That's unfortunate; she always appreciated my baked goods.
Found odd dents in my rolling pin this morning, like claw marks. Peculiar indeed.
I KNEW the barmaid was a werewolf; she always eyed my customers strangely while eating my bread.
THAT's IT! NO MORE PASTRIES! Until the werewolf has stopped. I have principles you know.

farmer.text: Last night, I was harvesting late crops for the full moon festival.
Picked up mended tools from the blacksmith last night. He was working feverishly.
The Blacksmith is a werewolf? That's certainly a setback for festival preparations.
Discovered trampled crops this morning, with large paw prints nearby. Unsettling.
The festival is fading... Well atleast I can focus on my potatoes again.

beggar.text: I love full moon festival! It's guaranteed to be a relaxing and peaceful time.
I saw the barmaid running around on all fours last night! Must be a new TikTok trend.
The barmaid was a werewolf? The scraps she gave me were a bit... Meaty!
I was hanging outside the Blacksmith's forge last night. He gave me scraps... that looked oddly fresh!
The barmaid was a werewolf? The scraps she gave me were a bit... Meaty!
I just can't sleep at night with those howls from the Smithing Forge. Must be a new type of alarm clock.
I just can't sleep at night with those howls from the Blue Moon Inn. Must be a new type of alarm clock.

mayor.text: I was awake until the early hours planning speeches and activities for the Full Moon Festival!
I stopped by the Blue Moon Inn last night to check on festival supplies. The barmaid was working hard as always.
The barmaid is gone? This is a tragedy for the festival! Well... Atleast she's not eating anyone.
The Blue Moon Inn is being strangley loud at the moment. Lots of noise at the strike of midnight!
I investigated the Blacksmith's forge last night. The howling is way past our village curfew!
Well, besides all the eaten people and werewolves. I'd say the Moon Festival was a success!

blacksmith.text: Oh me? I was just forging decorations for the Blue Moon Festival... I think it's going to be a good one!
I was with the barmaid last night collaborating on some... Creative festival Ideas.
The Barmaid gone? That's a pity. We were really getting along.
I just really like the way the moon looks at the moment. Must be the festivals festivities!
The Barmaid gone? That's a pity. We were really getting along.
The festival is over. Such a shame. The villagers wont come out late now.
I miss my savory escapades with the barmaid... I mean, successful... Successful escapades!

fisherman.text: Christmas is here! Secret Santa gifts are everywhere. I left a big fish for someone last night.
I saw the baker and beggar swap presents last night. Looked odd.
The beggar got my fish gift. He ate the wrapper too. I knew he was bad.
I knew the baker was a wolf. His present was a pie that smelled like meat, not fruit!
The baker gave everyone red cookies last night.
The beggar stole gifts from under the tree. I saw him run off.
The baker keeps saying his oven is hot for fresh meat. Not cookies!
Christmas is ruined. At least I still have my fish.

butcher.text: I gave meat gifts for Secret Santa. Big ham for someone last night.
I cut meat all night for presents, so I don't know anything. I promise!
The beggar asked for extra meat for him last night. He ate it raw.
I left a large Christmas ham under the Christmas tree. There were HUGE bites in it!
Well, my Christmas ham is gone. Atleast I wasn't eaten!

barmaid.text: I served hot drinks at the Blue Moon Inn for Christmas. The Secret Santa party was fun.
The baker and beggar swapped gifts last night. It looked... Meaty? Weird NGL.
Last night was Busy. But I heard growls near the Christmas tree.
Christmas cheer is low. I think it's because of all the people getting eaten.

baker.text: I baked Ginger Bread villagers for Secret Santa... Special recipe.
I left cookies last night. Tasted great. Fresh.
Oh dear... The Beggar is gone? No one to test my new meat cookies.
Me and the beggar shared gift ideas last night. We like meat in cookies! Extra chewy!
I must say, these villagers eating all these Christmas treats have made them FAR more delicious!
I miss night baking with beggar. Good eats. Grr... I mean good times!

farmer.text: I gave my prize vegetables for Secret Santa. I Left carrots last night.
Gave flour to baker last night. He said he was extremely hungry.
The Baker was a werewolf! No-one wants my carrots now.
I found bite marks on the vegetable gift bags I left under the Christmas tree. Enormous bites!
I wish these werewolves would just eat their vegetables.

beggar.text: It's secret Santa this year! I love surprises!
I wish someone would just gift me 50 kilograms of meat this year!
All these tasty villagers look like gifts to me!
This years Christmas has been one to remember. So many tasty memories.

mayor.text: Let's not let this small werewolf issue bring us down! It's CHRISTMAS!
Ho Ho Ho! Let's keep up the Christmas cheer!
Christmas cheer is still here... I assure you...
Nevermind Christmas! This is a disaster. Bring on summer!

blacksmith.text: The werewolves better not ruin Secret Santa this year!
The beggar was snooping around the tree the other night. Looked strange.
That beggar was a werewolf! I would've never guessed.
The baker gave me these delicious meaty biscuits! He's a great guy.
The baker gave me these delicious meaty biscuits! He's a great guy.
To be honest. All the werewolves eating the villagers has made this Christmas a bit disappointing.

mayor.text: Last night I was inspecting the old mill. The council wants it torn down!
The farmer keeps blaming the mill spirits. Spirits don't leave paw prints!
I always said that mill was cursed, and the farmer knew it best!
I've ordered extra lanterns near the mill. Safety first!
A werewolf in MY village? [sighs] This is a governance nightmare.
Somebody is haunting more than that mill, mark my words.

butcher.text: [sighs] I was cleaning my counters till late. That mill creaks something awful at night.
The fisherman said he saw nothing from the river. From a river you see EVERYTHING.
The fisherman's gone? And here I thought he saw nothing from the river. Convenient.
Someone's been raiding my scrap bins. Big appetite, whoever it is.
The farmer, a werewolf?! No wonder his crops smelled of blood.
I sharpen my knives for a reason, you know.

baker.text: I was baking through the night. That mill provides all my flour!
The farmer delivered my flour late, muttering about spirits.
No farmer means no flour. This is a doughmestic crisis!
[nervously] I heard scratching at the mill wheel last night. That wasn't the wind.
My sourdough rises even when the village doesn't.

blacksmith.text: I was repairing the mill's iron gears all evening.
The fisherman borrowed a hook from me and never brought it back.
The fisherman a wolf? His nets were full of fur, not fish!
The mill gears had claw marks on them this morning.
Two wolves? [proudly] Good thing my forge can make silver.
Iron doesn't lie. People do.

beggar.text: I sleep by the mill for warmth. Last night the wheel turned with no water!
[whispering] I saw two shapes near the river. Farmer-sized and fisherman-sized.
Nobody believes a beggar until the howling starts.
Told you I hear everything! One of them's caught now.
Spare a coin, spare a life!

farmer.text: It wasn't me, it was the mill spirits! They come out every full moon, I swear.
I was guarding my crops all night. From spirits. Definitely spirits.
[nervously] Shame about the fisherman. We, uh, fished together sometimes.
That mill has been hungry for years. Not me. Never me.
Fine! The mill spirits and I have an... arrangement.
[clears throat] ...The wind sounds awful howly tonight, doesn't it?

fisherman.text: I was on the river all night and saw absolutely nothing. Nothing at all.
The river was calm. My belly, however, was rumbling.
The farmer gone? We had such... tasty times by the mill.
You can't prove I left the river. The current's my alibi!
[gulps] Alright, my catch last night wasn't exactly fish.
[licks lips] Fresh villager— I mean, fresh AIR by the river!

barmaid.text: The inn was dead quiet. Everyone's too scared of the mill.
The farmer and fisherman shared a booth, whispering all night.
The farmer drank three ales and kept howling. Should've clocked it sooner.
I serve drinks, not alibis. Someone here is lying.
One wolf down. Iconic. So who's the plus one?
[sighs] Bombastic side eye to whoever's ruining my tips.

mayor.text: I declared the frozen lake off-limits after last night's... incident.
Someone left tracks across the ice. Big, clawed tracks.
Those footprints to the lake? The butcher's boots, no doubt!
A mayor must keep his village from thawing into chaos!
I've never trusted a quiet frozen lake.

butcher.text: My footprints by the lake? I, uh, was ice fishing. For meat. Lake meat.
Cold weather is great for keeping produce fresh. [chuckles]
The blacksmith's gone? We had such crunchy midnight walks.
Prove those boots are mine! Everyone wears boots!
[gulps] Okay, those weren't fishing tracks.
[licks lips] Fresh cuts, best served cold.

baker.text: I skated to the lake to cool my ovens. It was eerily silent.
The blacksmith's hammering kept me up till dawn.
The blacksmith?! His tools smelled of wet dog. Now I get it.
My bread froze solid out there. Not my finest batch.
A crusty loaf beats a clawed villager any day.

blacksmith.text: Scratches on my tools? That's just... vigorous smithing. Very vigorous.
I was at the forge all night. The cold makes iron sing.
The butcher's gone? A shame. We shared everything. Even midnight snacks.
My tools scratch themselves! It's the frost, I tell you!
[nervously] Fine, those scratches weren't from a hammer.
[low growl] ...The forge fire keeps me warm. Very warm.

beggar.text: I hid from the cold by the lake and saw two figures on the ice!
Two sets of footprints, and neither stopped to help a beggar.
See? I told you the ice hides secrets. One's caught now!
I found a tuft of grey fur frozen to the dock.
Spare a coin, it's freezing out here!

farmer.text: My animals wouldn't cross the lake path. They sensed something.
The frost killed my winter carrots. Rude.
I found tufts of grey fur frozen in the reeds.
TWO wolves? On my frozen fields? Unbelievable.
Farmers know when nature's gone wrong. And it has.

fisherman.text: I couldn't fish, the lake was frozen over solid!
The butcher asked me the thickest part of the ice. Weird question.
The butcher by the lake? He wasn't fishing, that's for sure.
No fish, no dinner. Tragic week for me.
At least I stayed on dry land. Mostly.

barmaid.text: Nobody came to the inn, they all slipped on the ice!
The blacksmith and butcher left together, boots crunching.
The blacksmith gone means no one fixes my broken tap. Ugh.
Two people are lying and I've got the receipts.
One frosty wolf caught! Slay. Literally.
[sighs] My cocktails are colder than this mystery.

mayor.text: I've, ahem, misplaced some village records. Nothing suspicious!
As mayor, I keep certain attack reports confidential. For morale!
The fisherman gone? We shared many... late night stories.
A mayor's paperwork is sacred! Stop snooping!
[gulps] Those records may have mentioned my... nightly habits.
[clears throat] The moon does strange things to a man. Allegedly.

butcher.text: The fisherman keeps telling that lost-eye tale. Different every time!
The mayor won't let me see the attack records. Why hide them?
The mayor gone? Now who hides the reports? Suspicious timing.
I keep my cleaver close during these howly nights.
Meat's honest. Politicians aren't.

baker.text: The fisherman told me he lost his eye to a 'big grey fish'. Sure.
I baked eye-shaped buns for the festival. Bit on the nose, I know.
That eye story gives me the creeps every single time.
A grey FISH took his eye? More like he grew fangs!
My pastries never lie about their fillings.

blacksmith.text: I forged the fisherman a fine eyepatch clasp last week.
The mayor asked me to seal a strongbox. Full of papers, he said.
The MAYOR a wolf? No wonder those records vanished!
Something scratched my forge door at midnight.
Iron sees what politicians hide.

beggar.text: I heard the mayor burning papers behind town hall last night!
Nobody hides paperwork unless it bites back.
Told you the records were hiding a wolf!
I saw the fisherman's 'missing eye' glow in the dark. Just saying.
Spare a coin for an honest witness!

farmer.text: My scarecrow lost an eye last night too. Coincidence?
The mayor's new curfew keeps me off my own fields.
I found claw marks on the town hall shutters.
Two wolves running the village? I'm moving to the barn.
Crops don't tell tall tales. Fishermen do.

fisherman.text: Gather round! Let me tell you how I lost my eye to the beast of the deep...
The creature that took my eye had such... appetite. I admired it.
The mayor's gone? We had such a lovely understanding, he and I.
You doubt my eye story? The scars are REAL, friend.
[nervously] Alright, the 'beast' and I are more alike than I let on.
[licks lips] The deep is hungry tonight. So am I.

barmaid.text: The fisherman told his eye story six times. I counted.
The mayor kept a locked briefcase by his booth all night.
The mayor drank alone, muttering about the moon. Red flag!
Two liars in my inn and I'm this close to naming them.
One down! The tea is finally spilling.
[sighs] Major bombastic side eye to the storyteller.

mayor.text: The harvest festival must go on, werewolves or not!
The baker's new loaf tastes... gamey. What's in it?
No baker means the festival bread is cancelled. Tragic!
A golden harvest brings out the village's true colours.
I'll cut the ribbon myself. Carefully.

butcher.text: The baker asked me for 'special mince' for his bread. Odd order.
The farmer wouldn't let anyone near his fields last night.
The FARMER? He guarded those crops a little too fiercely!
I know meat, and that bread had meat in it.
[knife sharpening] Just prepping for the feast.

baker.text: My new harvest loaf has a secret ingredient. You'd never guess!
The reddish tint? Just, um, beetroot. Definitely beetroot.
The farmer gone? We had such a fruitful... partnership.
My recipe is a family secret! Stop sniffing my dough!
[gulps] Okay, the mince wasn't from a cow.
[licks lips] Fresh bread, fresh... filling. Delicious.

blacksmith.text: I sharpened the harvest scythes. The farmer wanted them EXTRA sharp.
Something big trampled the wheat rows in the night.
The baker's oven smelled like a slaughterhouse this morning.
Two wolves at the harvest? Time to forge silver sickles.
Iron for the fields, silver for the beasts.

beggar.text: I slept in the wheat and heard chewing all night. Not mice.
The baker and farmer met in the field at midnight. I saw!
See? The harvest hid a wolf! One's caught now.
That red bread left crumbs shaped like... teeth.
Spare a coin for the village crier!

farmer.text: I protect my crops with my LIFE. And my claws— er, my hoe.
Nobody touches my fields at night. Nobody LIVES to. Ahem.
The baker gone? Shame. We shared such fresh ingredients.
I guard the harvest, that's all! A farmer's duty!
[nervously] Those weren't scarecrow prints in the mud.
[low growl] ...The wheat whispers to me. It says 'feed'.

fisherman.text: I traded fish for the baker's bread. Regretted it instantly.
The baker's bread had a funny red swirl in it.
That baker's loaf bit ME back! Should've known!
I'll stick to the river, thanks. Safer than the bakery.
No harvest for me, just honest fish.

barmaid.text: Everyone's raving about the baker's red loaf. I think it's cursed.
The farmer and baker toasted to a 'bountiful hunt'. Weird toast.
The farmer sat growling into his cider. Big yikes.
Two of them are lying and it's giving guilty.
One caught! The harvest tea is delicious.
[sighs] I'm not serving that bread in MY inn.

mayor.text: The village has gone eerily silent. Even the dogs won't bark.
The beggar claims to hear everything. Perhaps he hears too much.
The beggar gone? He knew too many secrets, that one.
Silence in a village means someone's keeping quiet.
I'll restore order, one hushed street at a time.

butcher.text: Nobody bought meat today. The whole village is whispering.
The barmaid's new cocktail made three men sleep till noon.
The BARMAID? Those midnight drinks knocked people right out!
Quiet villages make me nervous. And I don't get nervous.
[knife tap] Sharpening keeps the silence company.

baker.text: Not one customer today. My bread went stale in silence.
The barmaid asked to borrow my darkest rye. For a 'drink', she said.
I heard a single howl cut through the silence at midnight.
Two wolves whispering in the dark? No wonder it's so quiet!
Even my sourdough is holding its breath.

blacksmith.text: My forge was the only sound in the whole village last night.
The beggar was lurking outside every window, listening.
The beggar a wolf? He 'overheard' secrets he was CAUSING!
Silence this thick usually means claws are out.
Iron speaks when the village won't.

beggar.text: I hear every secret in this town. [whispering] Every single one.
People tell me things. Then people... disappear. Funny that.
The barmaid gone? We shared such quiet midnight... meals.
A beggar hears all and tells nothing! Leave me be!
[gulps] Maybe I hear so much because I'm always out at night.
[licks lips] Secrets taste better than coins.

farmer.text: My animals are silent. They only go quiet when a predator's near.
I found paw prints leading to the inn's back door.
Two shadows crossed my field without a sound.
One wolf unmasked! Maybe now my cows will moo again.
Nature's silence is louder than any howl.

fisherman.text: Even the river seemed to hush last night. Unnatural.
The barmaid served me something that tasted of iron.
The barmaid's midnight drink? I woke up with fur on my coat!
I kept quiet and kept my oars close.
Silence and I are old fishing buddies.

barmaid.text: My midnight special? [nervously] It's a... family recipe. Very relaxing.
A good drink makes villagers sleep SO deeply. Convenient for me.
The beggar gone? Pity. He knew when to keep quiet. Now he always will.
My drinks are perfectly innocent! Ask anyone who woke up!
[gulps] Fine, the 'special ingredient' isn't exactly legal.
[licks lips] Last call, darlings. For some of you.

mayor.text: I ordered urgent repairs on the old castle. For, uh, historical reasons.
The castle needs restoring. Ignore the digging noises at night.
The blacksmith gone? We explored those tunnels together, sadly.
A mayor beautifies the village! Stop questioning the budget!
[gulps] Perhaps I ordered those tunnels for... personal use.
[clears throat] The castle and I share many secrets. Ahem.

butcher.text: The mayor's castle repairs cost a fortune. Where's it all going?
The blacksmith keeps hauling dirt from the castle at night.
The blacksmith dug tunnels? Perfect for a wolf to prowl!
I keep my cleaver handy near that spooky old keep.
Stone walls hide more than damp.

baker.text: I delivered bread to the castle workers. Cold, creepy place.
Someone's been tunneling under my bakery cellar too!
I heard scratching beneath the floorboards last night.
Two wolves with a castle full of tunnels? We're doomed!
My yeast rises, my courage doesn't.

blacksmith.text: I found hidden tunnels under the castle. Fascinating. Also mine now.
Those tunnels lead everywhere. Very handy for... late strolls.
The mayor gone? Our little tunnel project ends here, I suppose.
I just REPAIR the castle! The tunnels were already there!
[nervously] Fine, I dug those tunnels to move around unseen.
[low growl] ...The dark down there suits me.

beggar.text: I sleep in the castle ruins. Last night the walls MOVED!
I saw the mayor and blacksmith vanish into a wall. Poof!
Told you the castle was cursed! One wolf caught!
There's fresh dirt and fur all through those tunnels.
Spare a coin for a castle ghost survivor!

farmer.text: My sheep won't graze near the castle anymore.
The tunnel digging shook my potato field loose.
Two shady figures carried shovels toward the keep.
One wolf down! Maybe my sheep will calm down now.
Even the castle crows look nervous.

fisherman.text: The castle moat connects to my river. Something swam through it.
The mayor asked me the depth of the moat. Odd for a landlubber.
The mayor swimming the moat at midnight? Now it makes sense!
I fished a torn cloak out of the water. Muddy and clawed.
I'll keep to the river's edge, thanks.

barmaid.text: The castle workers drank at my inn, whispering about tunnels.
The blacksmith and mayor left together, covered in dust.
The blacksmith bragged about his 'secret tunnels'. Should've listened!
Two of them reek of damp stone and lies.
One down! This castle drama is delicious.
[sighs] I'm putting a lock on MY cellar tonight.

mayor.text: Complaints of howling near the river all night. Most disruptive!
The fisherman and beggar are always by that river. Suspicious pair.
The fisherman gone? The river's gone quiet too. Telling.
I'll station a guard by the water. If I can find a brave one.
A mayor's sleep matters too, you know!

butcher.text: Those river howls kept my dogs whining all night.
The fisherman smelled of wet dog when he sold me eels.
The fisherman howling by the river? Fishy indeed!
I keep the cleaver close when the howling starts.
Nothing honest howls at the moon.

baker.text: I couldn't sleep with all that howling down by the river!
The beggar asked me for 'raw' bread dough last night. Raw?!
The howls came in pairs. Like a duet. A scary duet.
Two wolves by the river? I'm baking with the doors bolted!
My bread rose with fear last night.

blacksmith.text: I forged a lantern hook for the river path. It's too dark down there.
The beggar and fisherman huddle by the river every night.
The beggar a wolf? He was always 'resting' right where the howls were!
I found claw marks on the river bridge railings.
Silver lanterns for dark river nights.

beggar.text: Me, by the river? I just rest there. [nervously] It's peaceful. Mostly.
The fisherman and I are just friends. Who happen to howl. Er, talk.
The fisherman gone? We had such howling good nights together.
A beggar sleeps where he can! The river's free!
[gulps] Alright, the howling might've been... me. A little.
[licks lips] The river brings such fresh... visitors.

farmer.text: The river howls spooked my cattle into the next county!
I found two sets of paw prints along the muddy bank.
The howls always came from the fisherman's spot.
One river wolf caught! My cows send their thanks.
Rivers carry secrets downstream.

fisherman.text: Howling? By the river? I heard nothing over my fishing. Nothing!
The beggar keeps me company by the water. We, um, sing.
The beggar's gone? Pity. He was such good company on hungry nights.
You can't pin river howls on an honest angler!
[gulps] Fine, that howling wasn't a wolf. It was TWO.
[licks lips] The river's dinner washes right up to me.

barmaid.text: Customers won't walk the river path home. Bad for business!
The fisherman and beggar always leave together at closing.
The fisherman left howling drunk toward the river. Clocked it!
Two of them share more than a fishing spot, I reckon.
One howler caught! The plot thickens like my stew.
[sighs] I'm adding a river surcharge to their tabs.

mayor.text: The bakery bell rang at midnight again. Who rings a bell at MIDNIGHT?
The baker swears he doesn't ring it. Then who does?
No baker means no midnight bell. Peaceful, if grim.
A ringing bell is a signal. But to whom?
I'll have that bell confiscated by decree!

butcher.text: That midnight bell woke the whole street. My sausages curdled.
The blacksmith repairs that bell weekly. It's never broken!
The blacksmith 'fixing' the bell so often? He was signaling!
I keep the cleaver by the door when it chimes.
Bells and butchers both mean business.

baker.text: My bell rings at midnight? [nervously] Must be... the wind. Strong wind.
The bell calls me to bake. At midnight. For reasons.
The blacksmith gone? He kept my bell in such good working order.
Leave my bell alone! A baker keeps odd hours!
[gulps] Okay, the bell isn't for baking. It's a... signal.
[licks lips] The midnight bell means dinner's ready.

blacksmith.text: I repair the bakery bell often because it, uh, breaks often. Trust me.
I keep that bell tuned to a very specific... midnight tone.
The baker gone? Who'll ring our little midnight bell now?
A blacksmith maintains things! That's my JOB!
[nervously] Fine, I tuned the bell to call the pack.
[low growl] ...The bell and I have an understanding.

beggar.text: I sleep under the bell tower. That midnight ring nearly deafened me!
Every time the bell rings, a shadow slips out the bakery.
Told you the bell was a wolf signal! One's caught!
The baker and blacksmith meet under the bell after it rings.
Spare a coin for the bell's only witness!

farmer.text: The midnight bell sends my roosters into a frenzy!
I found grey fur snagged on the bell rope.
The bell rings, then the howling starts. Every time.
Two wolves with a signal bell? Absolute chaos.
My animals hear the truth before we do.

fisherman.text: The bell carries all the way to the river. Eerie at midnight.
The baker asked me for a rope 'to fix the bell'. Fishy.
The baker rings that bell then goes hunting? Makes sense now!
I'll cast my nets far from that bell tower.
Bells at midnight are never good news.

barmaid.text: Last orders, then that awful bell drowns out my goodbyes!
The blacksmith and baker always vanish when the bell rings.
The blacksmith timed his 'repairs' to midnight exactly. Sus!
Two of them jump every time that bell chimes. Guilty.
One bell-ringer caught! Ding dong, the wolf is found.
[sighs] I'm soundproofing my inn. Enough is enough.

mayor.text: A 'shadow market' has appeared after dark. Unlicensed! Unacceptable!
The butcher sells meat I've never approved. What meat IS it?
No butcher, no shadow market. Case closed? Perhaps.
I'll regulate this midnight market into oblivion!
Commerce in shadows breeds trouble.

butcher.text: My special midnight cuts? [nervously] Er, exotic imports. Very exotic.
Business booms when the barmaid keeps everyone... looking away.
The barmaid gone? She kept the crowds SO nicely distracted for me.
A butcher sells MEAT! Stop asking where it's from!
[gulps] Fine, that meat wasn't beef. Or pork. Or legal.
[licks lips] Freshest cuts in the village. Trust me.

baker.text: The shadow market undercut my bread stall! Rude and shady.
The butcher's midnight meat had a strange, pale look.
The butcher's 'special meat' was villager-shaped, wasn't it?!
I saw fur, not leather, on that market stall.
Two wolves running a secret market? I'm appalled!
I'll only sell in broad daylight, thank you.

blacksmith.text: Someone bought ALL my meat hooks for the shadow market.
The barmaid handed out free drinks while the market ran. Convenient.
The barmaid distracting the crowd? She was covering the butcher!
I forged those hooks for meat. Not... this.
Iron tools, dark purposes.

beggar.text: I lurk at the shadow market. The 'meat' there GROWLS sometimes.
The butcher and barmaid run that stall like clockwork.
See? The market hid a wolf! One's caught now.
I found a villager's shoe behind the meat cart. Just a shoe.
Spare a coin, I'll keep your secrets!

farmer.text: My livestock keeps 'going missing' near the shadow market.
I never sold the butcher that much meat. So where's it from?
Two figures haul heavy sacks from the market at dawn.
One market wolf caught! My herd can rest easy.
A farmer counts his animals. The numbers don't add up.

fisherman.text: The shadow market wouldn't buy my fish. 'We deal in RED meat,' they said.
The butcher waved me off like he was hiding something.
The butcher's red meat was a bit TOO fresh, if you ask me.
I'll sell my catch at the honest docks, thanks.
Shadows and markets don't mix well.

barmaid.text: Distracting the crowd? [nervously] I just... entertain. That's my job!
A few free drinks and nobody notices what the butcher's selling.
The butcher gone? Our little market partnership is finished.
I pour drinks, I don't run scams! How dare you!
[gulps] Fine, the distraction was ON PURPOSE.
[licks lips] Another round to keep those eyes off the stall.

mayor.text: I'm hosting a moonlight race through the deep dark woods! For fun!
The race runs at midnight. Through the woods. Alone. Enjoy!
The farmer gone? He designed our lovely little race route.
A civic race builds community spirit! Nothing sinister!
[gulps] Perhaps the race route leads runners... to me.
[clears throat] May the fastest villager survive— er, win!

butcher.text: A midnight race through wolf-country? Whose idea was that?
The mayor's race conveniently ends where the attacks happen.
The mayor sends us into the woods at night? He's the WOLF!
I'll run that race with my cleaver, thank you very much.
Nobody herds sheep into a wolf den by accident.

baker.text: I made energy bread for the racers. They'll need it out there.
The farmer keeps changing the route toward the darkest woods.
No farmer means no race route. Small mercy.
I heard howls along the race path last night.
The mayor AND the farmer? They rigged the whole race!
My bread fuels runners, not wolves. Hopefully.

blacksmith.text: I forged the race trophy. Solid iron. Might double as a weapon.
The farmer marked the trail with strange bloody flags.
The farmer controlled the route straight into wolf territory!
Claw marks lined the race path this morning.
A trophy for the swift, silver for the beast.

beggar.text: I hide along the race route. Runners go in. Not all come out!
The mayor and farmer walked the route together at dusk.
Told you the race was a trap! One wolf caught!
I found a runner's number pinned to a torn, muddy jacket.
Spare a coin for the race's lone witness!

farmer.text: I control the race route. Naturally. I know these woods... intimately.
I routed the race through my favourite hunting— er, jogging spot.
The mayor gone? Our little race scheme dies with him.
I just know the land! A farmer plans a good trail!
[nervously] Fine, the route leads exactly where I want it to.
[low growl] ...The woods are so lively on race night.

fisherman.text: The race crosses my river bridge. I watched runners sprint past, terrified.
The mayor fired the starting horn then disappeared. Odd.
The mayor started the race then vanished into the trees. Sus!
I'll stick to my boat. No woods for me.
Rivers don't have wolves. Woods do.

barmaid.text: The whole village entered the moonlight race. My inn's empty!
The farmer and mayor toasted to a 'successful race'. Creepy.
The farmer bragged he 'designed the route for the hunt'. HELLO?!
Two of them planned this race a little too eagerly.
One racer-wolf caught! The finish line of justice!
[sighs] Next time the race ends at MY bar.

mayor.text: Mining tools and fishing gear found together at the old cave. Curious.
The blacksmith's tools by a CAVE? He's no miner.
No blacksmith to explain those tools now. Convenient.
I'll seal that mine before anyone else wanders in.
Forgotten places hide unforgotten crimes.

butcher.text: Why would fishing rods be at a dry cave? Makes no sense.
The fisherman's nets were found deep in the mine. Weird.
The fisherman at the CAVE not the river? He's the wolf!
Cleaver's coming with me if we search that cave.
Tools lie where their owners hunt.

baker.text: I brought bread to the cave searchers. Spooky echoes down there.
Something in that mine smelled like a wet, hairy dog.
I heard growling echo from the mine shaft.
Two wolves denning in a mine? That's their lair!
My loaves don't do caves. Too damp.

blacksmith.text: My tools at the cave? I was, um, prospecting. For iron. At night.
The mine's the perfect quiet spot for... personal projects.
The fisherman gone? We shared that cozy little cave, he and I.
A smith looks for ore! The cave is FULL of it!
[nervously] Fine, the cave's our den. Mine and the fisherman's.
[low growl] ...The dark of the mine feels like home.

beggar.text: I shelter in that mine sometimes. Last night it was OCCUPIED.
I saw the blacksmith and fisherman slip into the cave at moonrise.
Told you the mine had monsters! One's caught!
There's a nest of fur and bones deep in the shaft.
Spare a coin for a homeless cave-dweller!

farmer.text: My goats grazed near the mine and came back trembling.
I found paw prints leading straight into the cave mouth.
Two people left the mine dragging something heavy.
One mine-wolf caught! My goats can graze again.
Animals avoid that cave for good reason.

fisherman.text: My gear at the cave? I, uh, was cave-fishing. It's a thing. Trust me.
The mine's near the river. Handy for washing off... evidence.
The blacksmith's gone? Our mine hideout feels empty now.
You can't blame a man for leaving a net somewhere!
[gulps] Alright, I don't fish in that cave. I HUNT from it.
[licks lips] The cave keeps my catch nice and hidden.

barmaid.text: The blacksmith and fisherman drank together, whispering about a 'mine'.
Those two always leave toward the cave, never the river.
The blacksmith kept muttering about his 'den'. Clocked it now!
Two of them share a secret cave. And a secret, clearly.
One caught! This mine mystery is unraveling nicely.
[sighs] Who picks a dusty mine over MY warm inn? Suspicious.

mayor.text: Removing village records? Just... spring cleaning. In the archive. At night.
The records are being reorganized. Nothing about attacks, I assure you!
The baker gone? He lit such lovely candles for our... meetings.
A mayor manages archives! Stop rifling through my paperwork!
[gulps] The records I burned mentioned some... nightly incidents.
[clears throat] What the village forgets can't hurt it. Heh.

butcher.text: The baker lights candles every single night. For what, exactly?
The mayor took the attack ledgers. Why hide the count?
The mayor burned the records! Hiding his own wolfy tracks!
I keep my shop candlelit AND cleaver-ready.
Light hides as much as darkness.

baker.text: I light candles nightly. For, um, ambiance. Baking ambiance. [nervously]
The candles in my window mean the coast is... clear. For baking!
The mayor gone? Who'll I signal with my candles now?
A baker likes a cozy glow! Leave my candles be!
[gulps] The candles are a signal. To meet. You've got me.
[licks lips] One candle means the oven's hot. And hungry.

blacksmith.text: I made the baker a dozen candle holders. He burns through them fast.
The mayor asked me to melt down some 'old iron records'. Odd.
The mayor a wolf? No wonder he shredded the evidence!
Claw marks on the archive door this morning.
The baker's candles AND the mayor's cover-up? A pack in charge!
Iron remembers what paper forgets.

beggar.text: I watch the baker's candles from the gutter. They flicker in patterns!
When the baker lights two candles, the mayor sneaks out. Every time.
Told you those candles were a code! One wolf caught!
I saw the mayor toss burning papers in the river.
Spare a coin for the candle-watcher!

farmer.text: The baker's candlelight spooks my chickens through the window.
The mayor took MY land records too. Now I can't prove my own field!
Two shadows met by candlelight behind town hall.
One wolf unmasked! Maybe I'll get my records back.
Burned records smell like guilt to me.

fisherman.text: I fished up half-burned village records from the river!
These soggy papers list every night attack. Someone hid them.
The mayor dumped these in the water. Covering his tracks!
The baker's candle reflected on the water all night.
The river gives up every secret eventually.

barmaid.text: The mayor drank alone, shredding papers into my fireplace. Rude!
The baker and mayor exchanged a candle like a secret handshake.
The baker slipped out the second his candles were lit. Sus!
Two of them are burning more than the midnight oil.
One down! The records mystery is heating up.
[sighs] Bombastic side eye to whoever's torching evidence in MY hearth.

mayor.text: A storm last night, yet the attacks continued. Rain won't stop a wolf.
The beggar shelters under bridges. Right where tracks were found.
The beggar gone? He knew every dry hiding spot in the rain.
I'll issue umbrellas AND a curfew. Order in all weather!
Rain washes away tracks. And alibis.

butcher.text: I never left my shop in that rain! [nervously] Not once. Bone dry, me.
Rain's perfect cover. Washes away all sorts of... mess. Allegedly.
The beggar's gone? We used to shelter together, rain-soaked.
A butcher stays with his meat! Rain or shine!
[gulps] Fine, my boots WERE muddy. I wasn't in the shop.
[licks lips] Wet weather keeps the cuts fresh.

baker.text: The rain flooded my flour cellar. Miserable night for baking.
The butcher's boots were soaked, but he swears he stayed in.
The butcher 'never left'? His shop floor was covered in mud!
I heard splashing footsteps and a howl in the downpour.
Two wolves out in the storm? No wonder the tracks were everywhere.
My bread's soggy and so is this alibi.

blacksmith.text: My forge nearly went out in that rain. Long, wet night.
The beggar was the only one who stayed dry. Suspiciously dry.
The beggar under the bridge? Prime spot for a wolf to lurk!
Claw marks in the mud by the bridge this morning.
Rust and rain reveal the truth.

beggar.text: Under the bridge? [nervously] Yes, staying DRY. That's all. Honest.
The rain hides my comings and goings. Very handy. Er, cozy.
The butcher gone? We sheltered under the same bridge, he and I.
A beggar hides from the rain! Is that a crime now?!
[gulps] The bridge isn't for shelter. It's for... waiting.
[licks lips] Rainy nights bring the tastiest wanderers.

farmer.text: The storm flooded my lower field. And washed up strange paw prints.
My dog barked at the bridge all night through the rain.
Two figures huddled under the bridge in the storm.
One soggy wolf caught! My dog can finally sleep.
Even the rain couldn't wash away those tracks.

fisherman.text: The river swelled in the storm. Dangerous fishing, but I braved it.
I saw two shapes under the bridge as the rain hammered down.
The butcher by the flooded bridge? He said he never left the shop!
Something with fur floated past my boat. Gave me chills.
A fisherman knows the river better than any liar.

barmaid.text: Nobody braved the storm to drink. Deadest night I've had.
The butcher and beggar both came in dripping wet. Both denied it.
The beggar came in soaked but 'hadn't been out'. Make it make sense!
Two of them lied about staying dry. I saw the puddles.
One rain-soaked wolf caught! Justice pours down.
[sighs] Muddy boots on my clean floor. The AUDACITY.

mayor.text: Reports of a 'secret garden' the farmer guards. On village land!
The farmer won't let me inspect his hidden garden. What grows there?
No farmer, no guarded garden. What was he hiding in there?
I'll survey that garden by decree. Nothing stays secret from me!
Secret gardens grow secret troubles.

butcher.text: The farmer guards that garden like it's full of gold. Or bones.
The barmaid sneaks to the garden every midnight. Why?
The barmaid visiting after midnight? She's in on it!
I'll bring my cleaver if we search that patch.
Nothing good grows in the dark.

baker.text: I asked the farmer for garden herbs. He slammed the gate in my face!
That garden smells of meat, not marigolds.
I heard chewing behind the garden hedge at midnight.
The farmer AND the barmaid meeting in secret? It's a wolf garden!
My herbs come from honest soil, thanks.

blacksmith.text: I forged the farmer's garden gate. He wanted it EXTRA strong. To keep things IN.
The farmer's gate had claw marks on the inside. Inside!
The farmer guarding a garden 'from wolves'? He IS the wolf!
Something big paces that garden at night.
Iron gates keep secrets both ways.

beggar.text: I peeked over the garden wall. There were BONES in the flowerbeds!
The barmaid climbs the garden wall every midnight. I've watched!
Told you that garden was grim! One wolf caught!
The farmer buries strange things among the cabbages.
Spare a coin for the garden's secret witness!

farmer.text: My secret garden? I guard it because... rare vegetables. Very rare. [nervously]
Nobody enters my garden but... certain trusted midnight guests.
The barmaid gone? Our midnight garden visits are over.
A farmer protects his crops! Stay off my land!
[gulps] Fine, I don't grow carrots back there.
[low growl] ...The garden feeds well under a full moon.

fisherman.text: The garden backs onto my river. I've seen odd midnight visitors.
The barmaid and farmer whisper by the garden gate nightly.
The barmaid rowed across to the garden at midnight! I saw her!
A gnawed bone washed down from the garden into my nets.
The river sees what the hedge hides.

barmaid.text: Midnight garden visits? [nervously] I just... love gardening. By moonlight.
The garden's the perfect place for a private midnight... feast. Of veg!
The farmer gone? Our secret garden loses its keeper.
A barmaid needs fresh air! The garden's lovely at night!
[gulps] Okay, I don't go there for the roses.
[licks lips] The garden's harvest is always... fresh.

mayor.text: I decreed a wolf-mask party! Everyone hides their face. Delightful!
A masked party means no one sees who slips out. How fun!
The blacksmith gone? He wore such a convincing wolf mask. Too convincing.
A mayor throws grand parties! Stop reading into it!
[gulps] My mask wasn't... entirely a mask. Ahem.
[clears throat] Best costume goes to the most... convincing wolf.

butcher.text: A wolf-mask party during a WOLF crisis? Tone deaf, mayor.
The mayor insisted everyone mask up. Awfully convenient.
The mayor threw the party to hide his OWN mask! Clever wolf.
I wore my mask AND kept my cleaver. Just in case.
Masks hide faces. And fangs.

baker.text: I baked wolf-shaped cookies for the masked party. In hindsight, grim.
The blacksmith's mask looked awfully real up close.
The blacksmith never took his mask off. Because it wasn't ONE!
Under the music, I swear I heard a real growl.
Two masked wolves at a wolf party? Hiding in plain sight!
My cookies were a bite-sized regret.

blacksmith.text: My wolf mask? [nervously] Best in the village. So lifelike, they say.
A mask means nobody knows when I slip away for a... snack.
The mayor gone? He threw the perfect party for us to blend in.
I forged the best mask, that's all! It's craftsmanship!
[gulps] Fine, I didn't NEED a mask to look like a wolf.
[low growl] ...Keep your mask on. It suits the mood.

beggar.text: They didn't invite me to the mask party. So I watched from outside.
Two masked figures slipped out mid-party and came back... bloody.
Told you a real wolf was under a mask! One's caught!
One 'mask' had actual fur under it. I SAW.
Spare a coin for the uninvited witness!

farmer.text: The whole village at a party while my sheep vanish? Typical.
I found a discarded wolf mask in my field. With real teeth marks.
Two guests left the party heading for my paddock.
One masked wolf caught! Party's over for the beast.
You can mask a face but not a hunger.

fisherman.text: I skipped the party. Masks give me the creeps, frankly.
I saw masked figures by the river during the party.
The mayor left his own party in a wolf mask. Toward the woods!
A wolf mask floated down the river at dawn. Ominous.
No masks on the water. Just honest faces.

barmaid.text: I catered the mask party. Couldn't tell who I was serving all night!
The blacksmith and mayor kept their masks on ALL night. Sus.
The blacksmith refused to unmask for his drink. Now I know why!
Two guests never showed their faces. Guilty energy.
One down! The masked ball of lies is unraveling.
[sighs] Next party has a strict no-mask policy.

mayor.text: The village lanterns keep vanishing near the river and bakery. Sabotage!
The fisherman and baker's areas lose the most lanterns. Coincidence?
With the fisherman gone, no more lanterns have vanished. Hmm.
No lanterns means darkness. And darkness means wolves.
Someone WANTS this village blind.

butcher.text: Dark streets are dangerous streets. Who's stealing the lanterns?
The fisherman's dock is pitch black now. Every lantern gone.
The fisherman kills the lanterns so he can hunt unseen!
I work by candlelight and keep my cleaver closer.
Thieves love the dark they create.

baker.text: Missing lanterns? [nervously] Terrible! I do all my baking by... moonlight now.
Fewer lanterns means fewer eyes on the bakery at night. Convenient!
The fisherman gone? He and I both preferred the dark, you know.
Why would a baker steal light? I NEED to see the dough!
[gulps] Fine, I snuffed the lanterns. Darkness suits my... work.
[licks lips] The dark makes everything taste better.

blacksmith.text: I forged those lanterns myself! Now they're vanishing. Insulting!
I found a smashed lantern behind the bakery. Deliberate.
The baker's street went dark first. He's hiding in it!
Claw marks on every lantern post near the river.
Two wolves killing the lights? They want total darkness!
I'll forge lanterns that CAN'T be snuffed.

beggar.text: The lanterns were my only light at night! Now I'm in the dark.
I saw the fisherman and baker snuffing lanterns, one by one.
Told you someone wanted it dark! One wolf caught!
They toss the lanterns in the river so no one finds them.
Spare a coin AND a candle, please!

farmer.text: Without street lanterns, my animals panic in the dark.
I found lantern glass smashed along the river path.
Two figures moved lantern to lantern, dousing each one.
One wolf caught! Bring back the lights already.
Darkness is a predator's best friend.

fisherman.text: Lanterns missing by MY river? [nervously] Shocking. I fish in the dark now.
No lanterns means no witnesses on the water. Er, I mean, romantic!
The baker gone? He liked the dark as much as I do. Did.
A lantern fell in the river! It happens! Currents!
[gulps] Fine, I drowned the lanterns. I hunt better blind.
[licks lips] Dark water, easy prey.

barmaid.text: My patrons won't walk home with all the lanterns gone!
The baker and fisherman both left as the last lanterns died.
The baker left carrying a 'broken' lantern. It wasn't broken before!
Two of them profit from the dark. I'd bet my best barrel.
One light-thief caught! Illuminating, truly.
[sighs] I'm hanging torches. Try snuffing THOSE.

mayor.text: I run the midnight market. For commerce! Whatever a villager needs at midnight, I supply.
I control who trades after dark. And what... disappears. Ahem.
The beggar gone? He traded such useful... secrets at my market.
A mayor regulates trade! There's nothing sinister here!
[gulps] Some of my market 'goods' had a pulse. Recently.
[clears throat] The midnight market never closes. For SOME customers.

butcher.text: The mayor's midnight market undercuts my meat with 'mystery cuts'.
The mayor lets only certain traders in after dark. Shady.
The mayor controls the market AND the disappearances. Wolf!
I keep my cleaver out at that market.
Midnight trade is rarely honest.

baker.text: I sold bread at the midnight market. The beggar bought it with SECRETS.
The beggar knows everyone's business. Dangerous man.
Something growled behind the market stalls.
The beggar AND the mayor? They run this whole dark market!
My bread's honest. Their trade isn't.

blacksmith.text: I sell tools at the midnight market. Odd crowd, that one.
The beggar whispers deals in every stall's shadow.
The beggar trades SECRETS? He knew who to hunt next!
I found claw marks on my market cart.
Iron for sale, secrets for free apparently.

beggar.text: I trade secrets at the market. [nervously] Everyone's got a price. And a scent.
I know who's alone at midnight. Very... useful information.
The mayor gone? He and I ran such a tidy little market.
A beggar deals in gossip, not blood! Back off!
[gulps] Fine, the secrets I trade help me pick my dinner.
[licks lips] The best secrets are the ones you eat.

farmer.text: My produce vanishes at that market and no coin ever appears.
I tracked paw prints from the market to the woods.
Two traders always leave together when the stalls close.
One market-wolf caught! I want my vegetables back.
Nothing at that market is what it seems.

fisherman.text: I sold fish at the midnight market. Nobody wanted fish. They wanted 'meat'.
The mayor and beggar huddled behind the stalls all night.
The mayor waved certain traders through, skipped the rest. Rigged!
A gnawed bone rolled out from under a market table.
I'll trade at the honest morning docks.

barmaid.text: The midnight market steals my late-night trade! And my customers vanish!
The beggar and mayor toasted a 'good night's trade'. Chilling.
The beggar sold a 'secret' then a villager went missing. Connected!
Two of them run that market like a hunting ground.
One caught! The midnight market's dark deals exposed.
[sighs] My inn closes at a DECENT hour, thank you.

mayor.text: The storm destroyed most evidence. But muddy footprints remain!
The footprints match the butcher's boots. And the farmer's.
No butcher, and yet those big boot prints stopped appearing. Hmm.
Mud tells the truth even when people don't.
A storm can't wash away guilt entirely.

butcher.text: Muddy footprints? [nervously] Everyone's boots are muddy in a storm!
The storm washes away everything. Very convenient for... reasons.
The farmer gone? We stomped through the mud together, he and I.
A butcher walks in mud like anyone else!
[gulps] Fine, those big prints by the barn are mine.
[licks lips] Storms make the cleanup so easy.

baker.text: The storm soaked my flour AND my nerves. What a night.
The farmer's boots were caked with fresh red mud.
The farmer's prints led from the barn to the bodies. He's the wolf!
I heard a howl crack louder than the thunder.
Two sets of prints in the mud? A pair of wolves!
My bread and my courage both got washed out.

blacksmith.text: The storm nearly flooded my forge. I barely kept the fire alive.
I matched the footprints to a boot I mended for the butcher.
The butcher's boots made those prints. I forged his boot-nails!
Claw marks under the mud by the barn.
Mud hardens into evidence.

beggar.text: I sheltered in the barn during the storm. It was NOT empty.
I saw the butcher and farmer tracking mud everywhere at midnight.
Told you the barn had a beast! One wolf caught!
The footprints turn from boots to PAWS halfway across the field.
Spare a coin for a soggy witness!

farmer.text: Muddy prints on MY farm? Well, it's a FARM. There's always mud. [nervously]
The storm's the perfect time for a farmer to be... out and about.
The butcher gone? We made such a mess in the mud together.
I work my land in all weather! Those are just my boots!
[gulps] Those prints change shape because... so do I.
[low growl] ...The mud remembers what the rain forgets.

fisherman.text: The storm made the river wild. I nearly lost my boat!
I saw two figures slipping through the mud toward the barn.
The farmer's muddy prints ran right past my dock. Toward the attacks!
Something washed downriver in the storm. Something furry.
Storms reveal what calm waters hide.

barmaid.text: Nobody came out in that storm. Except, apparently, the wolves.
The butcher and farmer both came in filthy, blaming the storm.
The butcher tracked mud into my inn then denied being out. Busted!
Two of them left mud clues all over MY floor.
One muddy wolf caught! The storm couldn't hide it.
[sighs] I've mopped this floor THREE times. Rude.

mayor.text: Strange wolf-shaped tools were found in the forge. Most alarming!
The blacksmith forges wolf-shaped implements. Why, exactly?
With the blacksmith gone, who made those wolf tools? A mystery.
I'll have that forge inspected top to bottom.
A craftsman reveals himself in his craft.

butcher.text: Wolf-shaped tongs? Wolf-headed hammers? The blacksmith's obsessed.
The blacksmith's new tools all look like fangs and claws.
The blacksmith forges wolves because he IS one!
I'll keep my own honest cleaver, thanks.
You forge what you love. Or what you are.

baker.text: The forge? I just, um, buy bread trays there. Normal trays. [nervously]
The blacksmith and I share the forge for late-night 'projects'.
The blacksmith gone? He forged such lovely... tools for us.
I'm a baker! I just collect my trays! Leave me be!
[gulps] Fine, my bread stamps are wolf-shaped for a REASON.
[licks lips] A wolf-stamped loaf, fresh and rare.

blacksmith.text: Wolf-shaped tools? [nervously] Just... an artistic phase. Very trendy.
I forge what inspires me. And lately, wolves inspire me. Deeply.
The baker gone? He so loved my wolf-stamped bread trays.
It's ART! A smith can have a theme!
[low growl] Fine, I forge wolves because I know them well.
[low growl] ...Every tool I make has a little bite.

beggar.text: I sleep near the forge for warmth. The tools in there GRINNED at me!
The baker and blacksmith hammer away in there past midnight.
Told you that forge was cursed! One wolf caught!
There's a wolf pelt hanging in the back of the forge.
Spare a coin for the forge's frightened witness!

farmer.text: The blacksmith made me a wolf-shaped plough. I didn't ask for that!
My horseshoes came back with little fangs on them. Unsettling.
I heard growling over the clang of the hammer.
The baker AND blacksmith at that forge? A wolf workshop!
Tools should help, not haunt.

fisherman.text: My fishing hooks from the forge were shaped like claws. Creepy!
The blacksmith wouldn't let me see the back of the forge.
The blacksmith's obsession with wolves? Now it all fits!
A clawed hook snagged something furry in the river.
I'll whittle my own hooks from now on.

barmaid.text: The baker and blacksmith drink together, sketching wolf designs. Weird hobby.
Those two vanish to the forge every night after last orders.
The baker doodled wolves on every napkin. Should've clocked it!
Two of them are far too into wolves for comfort.
One caught! The forge of lies is cooling down.
[sighs] Take your creepy wolf art OUT of my inn.

mayor.text: The village anniversary will be UNFORGETTABLE. I've planned everything.
The whole village gathered in one place at night. How convenient. Ahem.
The barmaid gone? She helped me plan such a... memorable feast.
A mayor honours tradition! This is a CELEBRATION, not a scheme!
[gulps] Perhaps the celebration was a trap. My trap.
[clears throat] To the village! May MOST of you see next year.

butcher.text: An anniversary feast during a wolf crisis? Gathering us like cattle.
The mayor scheduled the feast for the darkest night. Sus.
The mayor lured us all out at night. It's a HUNT, not a party!
I brought my cleaver to the celebration. Party favour.
A crowd is just a bigger buffet for a wolf.

baker.text: I baked the giant anniversary cake! Took me all night.
The barmaid served drinks that made everyone drowsy. Odd for a party.
The barmaid's 'celebration punch' knocked out half the guests!
Between toasts, I swear I heard howling.
The mayor AND the barmaid planned this? The party's a trap!
My cake survived. Not sure everyone did.

blacksmith.text: I forged the anniversary bell. Rang it myself at the feast.
The mayor kept eyeing the crowd like a menu.
The mayor gathered us all then slipped away. Classic wolf move!
Claw marks on the feast hall doors this morning.
Celebrations and traps ring the same bell.

beggar.text: They let me into the feast for once! Then people started vanishing.
The mayor and barmaid whispered a 'plan' behind the cake.
Told you the party was a trap! One wolf caught!
Guests went to the cellar for wine and never came back up.
Spare a coin, save a seat, watch your back!

farmer.text: The whole village at the feast means my farm's unguarded. Typical.
I found paw prints leading away from the feast hall.
Two hosts left the party at the exact same moment.
One party-wolf caught! Some anniversary this turned out to be.
A gathering is a gift to a hungry beast.

fisherman.text: I came up from the river for the feast. Wish I'd stayed on the water.
The barmaid poured everyone extra strong drinks. Suspicious.
The barmaid's punch had a funny... reddish tinge. And a bite.
A guest's scarf washed down my river at dawn. Torn.
The river never throws a deadly party.

barmaid.text: My anniversary punch? [nervously] A SPECIAL recipe. Everyone sleeps SO well after.
A drowsy crowd is an easy crowd. For clearing tables! Obviously.
The mayor gone? Our little celebration plan is ruined.
I just pour generous drinks! It's a PARTY!
[gulps] Fine, the punch was meant to make you all... easy pickings.
[licks lips] Bottoms up, darlings. This round's on the house.

mayor.text: A broken boat washed ashore, full of clues pointing to the forge.
The fisherman's boat broke apart, and inside were the blacksmith's tools!
With the fisherman gone, the boat mystery goes quiet.
Boats and forges shouldn't share secrets.
A wreck always tells a tale.

butcher.text: Why were forge tools hidden in the fisherman's boat?
The fisherman's boat had claw marks along the hull.
The fisherman ferried the blacksmith's wolf-tools by night!
Cleaver's ready if that boat holds more surprises.
Two trades, one dark secret.

baker.text: The wrecked boat smelled of iron and wet fur. Not fish.
I found a blacksmith's hammer wrapped in fishing nets. Odd pairing.
I heard howling from the direction of the wreck.
The fisherman AND the blacksmith? Their boat was a smuggling den!
My nose knows: that boat carried trouble.

blacksmith.text: My tools in the fisherman's boat? [nervously] I, uh, lent them. For repairs.
The boat was handy for moving things the forge shouldn't hold.
The fisherman gone? We rowed out together on... special nights.
A smith lends his tools! That's neighbourly!
[low growl] Fine, the boat carried more than tools.
[low growl] ...The water hides what the forge can't.

beggar.text: I slept in that boat before it broke. It was full of... bones.
I saw the fisherman and blacksmith row out at midnight, heavy-laden.
Told you the boat was grim! One wolf caught!
There's a wolf pelt tangled in the boat's netting.
Spare a coin for the shipwreck survivor!

farmer.text: The broken boat drifted into my flooded field. Full of strange gear.
Forge tools AND fishing nets, all bloodied. What were they doing?
Two figures abandoned the boat and fled into the dark.
One boat-wolf caught! Get that wreck off my land.
A farmer knows a cover-up when he steps in one.

fisherman.text: My boat broke? [nervously] A tragic accident. Nothing on board but... fish.
The boat let me move about unseen. Handy for a hungry— er, hardy angler.
The blacksmith gone? He and I shared that boat for our night runs.
Boats break! It's the RIVER'S fault, not mine!
[gulps] Fine, that boat wasn't hauling fish.
[licks lips] The water always brings me dinner.

barmaid.text: The fisherman and blacksmith always left together toward the docks.
Those two whispered about a boat and a forge every night.
The fisherman bragged about his 'night cargo'. Now the boat spills all!
Two of them shared a boat AND a secret. Guilty.
One caught! This shipwreck of lies is sinking fast.
[sighs] Take your smuggling gossip elsewhere.

mayor.text: Red bread from the baker, mystery meat from the butcher. I'm concerned.
The baker's bread is suspiciously RED. What's the ingredient?
No baker, no red bread. The village menu improves already.
Food this strange demands an investigation.
You are what you bake. And sell.
