butcher.text: My meat deliveries? [nervously] Perfectly normal cuts. Very... fresh.
I supply the baker special mince. Don't ask what kind. Heh.
The baker gone? He mixed my finest cuts into his red loaf.
A butcher delivers MEAT! Stop questioning my cuts!
[gulps] Fine, that meat wasn't from any animal you'd name.
[licks lips] Freshest delivery in the village, guaranteed.

baker.text: My red bread? [nervously] It's, um, a rare berry glaze. Very exotic.
The butcher's special mince gives my bread that lovely red hue.
The butcher gone? He gave me the perfect... filling for my loaf.
It's a SECRET RECIPE! A baker's allowed his mysteries!
[gulps] Fine, the red isn't beetroot. Or berries.
[licks lips] Red bread, best served warm and rare.

blacksmith.text: The baker and butcher deliver to each other at midnight. Odd hours.
I forged the butcher a new cleaver. He's been using it a LOT.
The butcher's 'meat' was villager, wasn't it? And the baker baked it!
Claw marks on the butcher's delivery cart.
The baker AND butcher, in cahoots? A whole wolf kitchen!
Iron cuts through the tastiest lies.

beggar.text: I begged for that red bread. It tasted... like a villager. I just know it!
The butcher wheels red parcels to the bakery every midnight.
Told you the bread was wrong! One wolf caught!
There were teeth marks in the loaf. Not MINE.
Spare a coin, but keep the red bread!

farmer.text: The butcher stopped buying MY livestock. So where's his meat from?
My missing sheep and his 'fresh delivery' started the same night.
Two carts rolled between the shop and bakery at midnight.
One caught! Maybe my sheep will stop vanishing now.
A farmer counts. And the count is wrong.

fisherman.text: I offered the baker fish for his bread. 'I only use RED meat,' he said.
The baker's bread had a swirl of something... fleshy.
The baker's red loaf bit back when I tore it! Cursed thing!
A bloody wrapper washed down my river from the bakery.
I'll stick to honest fish, thanks.

barmaid.text: Everyone raves about the red bread. I refuse to serve it.
The baker and butcher toast to their 'special partnership' nightly.
The butcher bragged his meat was 'the freshest in years'. EW, now I get it!
Two of them share a recipe I do NOT want to know.
One caught! This red bread mystery is fully baked.
[sighs] My inn is a strictly beige-bread establishment now.

mayor.text: The old barn stands empty, yet lights flicker in it at night.
The farmer owns that barn but swears it's abandoned. Is it?
With the farmer gone, the barn's finally dark. Interesting.
I'll have that barn searched from rafter to floor.
Empty barns make excellent hiding places.

butcher.text: Why does an 'empty' barn smell of blood and hay?
The farmer forbids anyone near his empty barn. Why?
The farmer's barn is his lair! That's where he stashes them!
I'll bring my cleaver to the barn search.
Nothing's ever truly empty.

baker.text: I stored flour in that barn once. Now the farmer's locked me out.
Something big shuffles in the barn loft at night.
I heard chewing and growling from the hayloft.
The farmer AND beggar in the barn? Their whole operation!
My flour's safer at the bakery now.

blacksmith.text: I forged the farmer a heavy barn lock. To keep things OUT, he said. Or in.
The beggar knows the barn's secrets. I've seen him slip inside.
The beggar 'sleeping' in the barn? He was GUARDING it!
Claw marks all over the barn door.
A locked barn hides a loud secret.

beggar.text: I sleep in the empty barn. [nervously] Empty except me. And the... stuff.
The barn's a great place to hide from prying eyes. And stash things.
The farmer gone? He let me stay in the barn. For our... arrangement.
A beggar needs shelter! The barn was EMPTY!
[gulps] Fine, I guard the barn. It holds evidence. Our evidence.
[licks lips] The barn keeps my leftovers nice and hidden.

farmer.text: My barn's empty. [nervously] Nothing in there. Definitely no... remains.
Nobody goes in my barn but me. And my trusted lookout.
The beggar gone? He kept watch over my barn so well.
It's MY barn! I can lock it if I want!
[gulps] The barn isn't empty. It's where I keep the evidence.
[low growl] ...The hayloft hides a multitude of sins.

fisherman.text: The barn backs onto my river. I've seen the beggar dragging sacks inside.
The farmer and beggar meet at the barn every midnight.
The farmer rows things across to the barn at night! Caught him!
A bloodied sack floated from the barn into my nets.
The river tells on the barn.

barmaid.text: The farmer and beggar toast to the 'empty barn' every night. Weird flex.
Those two vanish to the barn the moment I close up.
The beggar bragged the barn 'holds all his secrets'. NOW I listen!
Two of them guard that barn like it's full of gold. Or bodies.
One barn-wolf caught! The empty barn wasn't so empty.
[sighs] What's IN that barn? Actually, don't tell me.

mayor.text: I've asked villagers to gather firewood in the whispering woods. At night. For thrift!
The woods are perfectly safe! Ignore the whispers. And the fisherman.
The fisherman gone? He watched the woods so... attentively for me.
A mayor promotes self-sufficiency! Gather that wood!
[gulps] I send them into the woods because I'm... waiting there.
[clears throat] The woods whisper my name. How flattering. Ahem.

butcher.text: The mayor sends us into the whispering woods at night? Madness.
The mayor's woodland errand always ends near the attacks.
The mayor herds us into the trees where HE waits. He's the wolf!
I chop wood with my cleaver. Two birds.
Whispers in the woods are warnings.

baker.text: I gathered kindling in the woods. The trees seemed to... breathe.
The fisherman watches the woodland path, never blinking.
The fisherman lurking in the WOODS, not the river? He's stalking us!
I heard whispers turn to growls among the trees.
The mayor sends them in, the fisherman picks them off! A pair!
I'll gather my firewood at NOON, thanks.

blacksmith.text: I made axes for the woodland gathering. The mayor ordered a LOT of them.
The fisherman watches from the treeline every single night.
The fisherman haunts those woods. Why leave the river he loves?
Claw marks scar the trees along the path.
The woods keep the mayor's secrets.

beggar.text: I live in those woods! The whispers are real, and so are the SCREAMS.
I saw the mayor lead villagers in, and the fisherman follow.
Told you the woods were deadly! One wolf caught!
There's a clearing full of bones deep in the woods.
Spare a coin for the woodland witness!

farmer.text: My woodpile's gone and my workers won't enter those woods.
I found paw prints circling the gathering clearing.
Two figures moved through the trees, herding the others.
One wolf caught! Maybe the whispers will stop now.
The woods whisper the truth if you listen.

fisherman.text: Me, in the woods? [nervously] I was just... gathering wood. Away from my river.
The woods are quiet. Perfect for a patient watcher. Er, wood-gatherer.
The mayor gone? He sent me such lovely... company in the woods.
A man can leave his river for firewood! It's cold!
[gulps] Fine, I wait in the woods for the mayor's little deliveries.
[licks lips] The whispering woods always deliver dinner.

barmaid.text: Villagers come to my inn shaking after the woodland gathering.
The mayor and fisherman whispered about the woods all night.
The mayor toasted to 'a good hunt in the woods'. WHO SAYS THAT?!
Two of them love those deadly woods far too much.
One woods-wolf caught! The whispers were confessions.
[sighs] I'm not restocking firewood from THOSE trees.

mayor.text: Under the silver moon, howls echo between the inn and the forge.
The howls bounce from the barmaid's inn to the blacksmith's forge.
With the barmaid gone, the inn's gone quiet under the moon.
A silver moon reveals silver truths.
Two buildings, one howl. Curious.

butcher.text: The silver moon has everyone spooked. And the howling doesn't help.
The blacksmith's forge glowed all night under the silver moon.
The forge howls under the moon because the BLACKSMITH does!
Silver's good for more than moons, I hear.
Under a full moon, watch everyone.

baker.text: I bake by moonlight sometimes. That silver glow is eerie.
The barmaid's inn and the forge seemed to answer each other.
The barmaid howled along with the moon! Thought it was singing!
The howls always came right after last orders.
The barmaid AND blacksmith howling in harmony? A wolf duet!
My moonlit loaves came out oddly pale.

blacksmith.text: The forge under the silver moon? [nervously] I just work late. Very late.
The moon does something to a man at the forge. Something... hairy.
The barmaid gone? We howled such lovely duets, she and I.
A smith works odd hours! The moon means nothing!
[low growl] Fine, that wasn't the forge fire howling. It was me.
[low growl] ...The silver moon calls, and I answer.

beggar.text: I watch the silver moon from the gutter. The inn and forge HOWL back at it!
The barmaid and blacksmith signal each other across the square.
Told you the howls had owners! One wolf caught!
Both their windows glow, then go dark, then the howling starts.
Spare a coin under this silver moon!

farmer.text: The silver moon drives my animals wild. And the howling's worse.
Paw prints run straight between the inn and the forge.
Two shapes crossed the moonlit square, howling.
One moon-wolf caught! My herd can settle now.
A silver moon never lies to a farmer.

fisherman.text: The silver moon lit the whole river. And carried the howls to me.
The forge and inn traded howls all night across the square.
The blacksmith's howl echoed off the water. Unmistakable!
Something silver-furred slipped along the moonlit bank.
The moon shows what the dark hides.

barmaid.text: Howling from my inn? [nervously] That's just... rowdy customers. Under the moon.
The silver moon brings out something wild in me. And my regulars.
The blacksmith gone? Our moonlit duets are over.
My inn is loud, not lupine! There's a difference!
[gulps] Fine, that howl WAS me. The moon, you know how it is.
[licks lips] The silver moon pours the best nights.

mayor.text: A grand feast, yet clues to the attacks were hidden right in the food!
The baker's feast dishes hid the strangest ingredients.
No baker means no feast. And no more poisoned platters, perhaps.
I'll have every dish inspected before the next feast.
A feast can feed a village or a beast.

butcher.text: The feast used meat I never supplied. So where did it come from?
The baker's feast bread had a suspicious red center.
The baker's centerpiece loaf had a FINGER in it! He's the wolf!
I'll carve the roast myself, thank you.
You can hide a lot in a big enough pie.

baker.text: My feast dishes? [nervously] Every one a masterpiece. With a... special touch.
A feast is the perfect place to serve... unusual meat. Discreetly.
The barmaid gone? We plated such memorable courses together.
A baker garnishes! Stop dissecting my canapes!
[gulps] Fine, the mystery meat pie wasn't mystery to ME.
[licks lips] The feast's finest dish is always the freshest.

blacksmith.text: I forged the feast's carving set. The baker wanted extra-sharp blades.
The barmaid poured a wine that dulled everyone's senses.
The barmaid's feast wine put everyone to sleep. Then the baker served!
Claw marks on the feast platters this morning.
The baker AND barmaid catered a WOLF feast!
Sharp knives, dark feasts.

beggar.text: They gave me the feast scraps. There were BONES that didn't match the roast!
The baker and barmaid whispered over each dish before serving.
Told you the feast was foul! One wolf caught!
A villager's ring turned up in the stew. Just the ring.
Spare a coin, but I'll pass on the feast!

farmer.text: My prize pig went missing right before the feast. Coincidence?
The feast meat wasn't from any animal on MY farm.
Two caterers left the feast dragging heavy, dripping sacks.
One feast-wolf caught! Some banquet THAT was.
A farmer knows his meat. That wasn't it.

fisherman.text: I brought fish for the feast. The baker binned it for 'red meat'.
The baker's dishes smelled of iron, not herbs.
The baker's feast pie growled when I cut it! Cursed!
A napkin full of bones washed down my river from the feast hall.
I'll feast on honest fish, thanks.

barmaid.text: My feast wine? [nervously] Vintage. Makes everyone SO wonderfully drowsy.
A sleepy feast crowd notices nothing. Perfect for... plating.
The baker gone? Our feast partnership is finished.
I pour good wine! It's a FEAST! People relax!
[gulps] Fine, the wine was drugged. The baker's idea. And mine.
[licks lips] Another toast, and don't ask about the meat.

mayor.text: The village tournament begins! Feats of strength, all in good fun.
The farmer and butcher dominate every event. Suspiciously strong.
With the farmer gone, the tournament's oddly safer. Hmm.
A tournament reveals a village's true champions. And villains.
Competition brings out the beast in some.

butcher.text: The tournament? [nervously] I'm just... naturally strong. And fast. And fanged.
The crowd's noise covers a lot. Screams, for instance. Allegedly.
The farmer gone? We made such a fierce team in the ring.
A butcher's got muscle! That's the JOB!
[gulps] Fine, I'm not THAT strong. I have... help. From within.
[licks lips] The tournament crowds are packed with... contenders.

baker.text: I sold pastries at the tournament. Nervous crowd this year.
The farmer's strength this year is inhuman, frankly.
The farmer tore the log-split event apart. With his TEETH, nearly!
Between rounds, I heard growling from the competitors' tent.
The farmer AND butcher sweeping every event? They're a wolf team!
My pastries are the only honest thing here.

blacksmith.text: I forged the tournament trophies. And the weapons for the duels.
The butcher's grip crushed my iron test-bar. Impossible.
The butcher won the strongman by lifting a CART. He's no man!
Claw marks on the tournament arena posts.
Strength like that isn't earned. It's cursed.

beggar.text: I watched the tournament from the fence. Competitors keep vanishing!
The farmer and butcher slip away between every event.
Told you the tournament was a cover! One wolf caught!
There's a pile of torn tournament sashes behind the tent.
Spare a coin for the sideline witness!

farmer.text: My tournament strength? [nervously] Clean living. Fresh air. And, er, moonlight.
The tournament's chaos is the perfect cover for... slipping away.
The butcher gone? We dominated the games together, he and I.
I toss hay bales all day! Of course I'm strong!
[gulps] Fine, I don't win by muscle alone.
[low growl] ...The tournament brings out my competitive HUNGER.

fisherman.text: I entered the fishing contest. The farmer and butcher won everything ELSE.
The butcher and farmer never seemed to tire. All day.
The butcher out-swam ME. A BUTCHER. Something's very wrong!
A competitor's boot washed down my river, mid-tournament.
No fish cheats. People do.

barmaid.text: The tournament packed my inn! But two champions kept sneaking out.
The farmer and butcher toasted to 'the real competition, at night'.
The farmer downed a raw steak between events. RAW! Clocked it!
Two of them are winning by... unnatural means.
One champion-wolf caught! Disqualified, permanently.
[sighs] Next tournament, I'm checking everyone for fur.

mayor.text: I've been visiting the old lighthouse. For, ah, maritime administration. At night.
The lighthouse is official business! The fisherman merely assists.
The fisherman gone? We held such productive meetings at the lighthouse.
A mayor oversees the coast! The lighthouse is MINE to visit!
[gulps] The lighthouse is where I meet my... associate. To plan.
[clears throat] The lighthouse beam hides more than it shows.

butcher.text: Why does the mayor meet the fisherman at the lighthouse at midnight?
The lighthouse lit up during every night attack. A signal?
The mayor and fisherman scheme in that tower! Both wolves!
I'll climb that lighthouse with my cleaver if I must.
Secret meetings breed secret crimes.

baker.text: The lighthouse beam swept over my bakery all night. Couldn't sleep.
The fisherman and mayor climbed the lighthouse together at dusk.
The fisherman climbs that tower nightly. To WATCH for prey!
The lighthouse flashed a pattern, then the howling began.
The mayor AND fisherman up in that tower? Plotting the hunt!
My bread rose fine. My suspicions rose higher.

blacksmith.text: I repaired the lighthouse lantern. The mayor insisted it be BRIGHT.
The mayor asked me to grease the lighthouse door. For 'quiet visits'.
The mayor uses the lighthouse to signal his fisherman friend. Wolves!
Claw marks spiral up the lighthouse stairs.
A beacon can guide ships or gather wolves.

beggar.text: I shelter at the lighthouse base. The mayor and fisherman step over me nightly!
They flash the light, then someone in the village screams.
Told you those two were scheming! One wolf caught!
There are gnawed bones at the top of the lighthouse stairs.
Spare a coin for the lighthouse witness!

farmer.text: The lighthouse beam spooks my animals every time it passes.
I found paw prints leading from my field to the lighthouse.
Two figures climbed the lighthouse together at midnight.
One tower-wolf caught! Maybe I'll sleep now.
A light that hunts is no light at all.

fisherman.text: The lighthouse? [nervously] I keep the lamp lit. For safety. My OWN safety.
From the top, I can see every lonely villager. For rescue! Obviously.
The mayor gone? Our lighthouse meetings meant so much to me.
A fisherman minds the beacon! It's tradition!
[gulps] Fine, I use the lighthouse to spot my next... catch.
[licks lips] The lighthouse shows me exactly who's alone.

barmaid.text: The mayor and fisherman leave my inn toward the lighthouse every night.
Those two always take a 'lighthouse walk' at closing. Together.
The mayor let slip they 'plan by lighthouse light'. Plan WHAT?!
Two of them share that tower AND a secret, I'd wager.
One caught! The lighthouse scheme is exposed.
[sighs] A lighthouse date at midnight? In THIS economy of murder?

mayor.text: The baker's secret recipe was stolen. And oh, what strange ingredients!
The baker guards a recipe with ingredients I dare not name.
No baker, no secret recipe. Perhaps that's for the best.
I'll have that recipe examined by the council.
Some recipes should stay secret. Buried, even.

butcher.text: The baker's recipe calls for meat I've never sold him.
The stolen recipe listed 'fresh long pig'. That's not a farm animal.
The baker's secret ingredient was VILLAGER! I knew that bread was off!
I'll keep MY recipes to honest cuts.
A recipe reveals a cook's true taste.

baker.text: My secret recipe? [nervously] Stolen! Now everyone knows my... special ingredient.
The recipe's secret is the meat. Very... free-range. Heh.
The beggar gone? He fetched my rarest ingredients, you know.
It's a FAMILY recipe! Secret means SECRET!
[gulps] Fine, the ingredient wasn't chicken. Or pork.
[licks lips] The freshest ingredient makes the finest loaf.

blacksmith.text: The baker asked me to forge a lockbox for one 'recipe card'. Just one!
The beggar was seen sneaking from the bakery with a bloody sack.
The beggar stole the recipe? No, he DELIVERED the ingredients!
Claw marks on the bakery's recipe lockbox.
You lock up what you're ashamed of.

beggar.text: I 'found' the baker's recipe. [nervously] The ingredients are... unusual.
I fetch what the recipe needs. Don't ask where from.
The baker gone? I gathered his special ingredients. Fresh ones.
A beggar finds things! Maybe I found a recipe! So what?!
[gulps] Fine, I don't fetch flour. I fetch... the OTHER stuff.
[licks lips] The recipe's best ingredient walks on two legs.

farmer.text: The baker stopped buying my grain. But his bread's doubled in size!
Whatever's in that recipe, it's not from any field of mine.
I heard chewing from the bakery at midnight.
The baker AND beggar cooking together? A recipe for murder!
A farmer knows: that recipe skipped the farm.

fisherman.text: I offered the baker fish for his recipe. He wanted 'fresher meat'.
The recipe's ingredients smelled of the graveyard, not the garden.
The baker's mystery loaf had a fingernail in it! CASE CLOSED!
A recipe page washed down my river, stained red.
I'll keep to fish stew, thanks.

barmaid.text: Everyone wants the baker's secret bread. I want NO part of it.
The baker and beggar whisper over that recipe every night.
The beggar bragged he 'sources the special ingredient'. EW. Clocked it!
Two of them share a recipe I'd rather not taste.
One caught! The secret recipe is out of the oven.
[sighs] My kitchen uses BEEF. Like a normal establishment.

mayor.text: The blacksmith forges weapons, the butcher stockpiles meat. For what war?
The blacksmith's secret armory and the butcher's meat pile alarm me.
With the blacksmith gone, the weapon-hoarding stopped. Telling.
I'll requisition both their stores at once.
Weapons and meat make a grim pairing.

butcher.text: My meat stockpile? [nervously] Just... good business. Very fresh stock.
Plenty of meat and plenty of blades. A good combination. For... reasons.
The blacksmith gone? He armed us both so well, he did.
A butcher stockpiles MEAT! It's winter coming!
[gulps] Fine, the meat pile isn't all livestock.
[licks lips] Freshest stock in the village. Trust me.

baker.text: The blacksmith and butcher trade weapons for meat at midnight. Odd barter.
The blacksmith's newest weapons are shaped like fangs.
The blacksmith forged CLAW-blades! Because he grows his own!
I heard clanging AND growling from the forge.
The blacksmith AND butcher, armed and fed? A wolf arsenal!
My rolling pin's my only weapon, thanks.

blacksmith.text: My secret? [nervously] Just... a few extra blades. For collecting. Fang-shaped ones.
I forge what the night requires. Sharp things. Very sharp.
The butcher gone? We traded steel for meat, he and I.
A smith makes WEAPONS! That's the whole trade!
[low growl] Fine, the blades aren't the only weapons I've got.
[low growl] ...The best blade is the one you're born with.

beggar.text: I peeked in the forge. Weapons AND a pile of bones. Not a good combo!
The blacksmith and butcher swap sacks and blades nightly.
Told you those two were armed and dangerous! One caught!
There's a meat-hook armory in the back of the shop.
Spare a coin for the unarmed witness!

farmer.text: The butcher took my whole herd but the meat pile's TEN times bigger.
The blacksmith's 'tools' look more like weapons every day.
Two of them hauled armed sacks toward the woods.
One caught! Maybe my animals are safe now.
A farmer counts livestock. His numbers scream.

fisherman.text: The blacksmith made me a hook sharp enough to fell an ox. Overkill!
The butcher wheels reddish barrels to the forge each night.
The butcher's 'meat' twitched when I passed the shop. He's the wolf!
A cleaver washed down my river, still bloody.
Too many weapons for an honest village.

barmaid.text: The blacksmith and butcher plot over ale about 'the supply'. Sinister.
Those two toast to 'weapons and meat' every single night.
The blacksmith bragged his blades 'match his bite'. NOW I hear it!
Two of them are stocking up for a hunt, I'd bet.
One caught! Their little armory's exposed.
[sighs] No weapons in my inn. House rule. Effective immediately.

mayor.text: The river festival draws the whole village to the water at dusk.
The fisherman runs the festival, the barmaid the refreshments. Cozy.
With the fisherman gone, the festival lost its... predator. Hmm.
I'll station guards along the riverbank this year.
A festival by dark water invites dark deeds.

butcher.text: A river festival at DUSK during a wolf crisis? Reckless.
The fisherman scheduled the festival for the darkest hour.
The fisherman lured us all to HIS river. It's a hunting ground!
I'll bring my cleaver to the riverbank.
Crowds by the water are easy pickings.

baker.text: I sold festival bread by the river. Beautiful night, until the screaming.
The barmaid served drinks that left folk dizzy near the deep water.
The barmaid's river punch had everyone swaying at the water's edge!
Between the fireworks, I heard howling on the far bank.
The fisherman AND barmaid ran this festival? A trap by the river!
My festival loaves floated off. So did my nerves.

blacksmith.text: I forged the festival lanterns for the river floats.
The fisherman steered the floats toward the shadowy bends.
The fisherman knows exactly where the deep, dark water is. For DUMPING!
Claw marks on the festival dock this morning.
Lanterns on water can't light every shadow.

beggar.text: I watched the river festival from the bushes. Guests kept slipping under!
The fisherman and barmaid signaled each other across the water.
Told you the festival was a trap! One wolf caught!
There are torn festival ribbons snagged on the reeds.
Spare a coin for the riverside witness!

farmer.text: The whole village at the river means my farm's alone tonight.
I found paw prints leading from the festival to the water's edge.
Two hosts left the festival heading downriver, dragging something.
One river-wolf caught! Some festival THIS was.
A gathering by dark water is a beast's buffet.

fisherman.text: My river festival! [nervously] Everyone gathers at MY water. How... convenient.
I know every deep, quiet bend of this river. Handy for... clean-up.
The barmaid gone? We ran such a memorable festival together.
I HOST the festival! That's hospitality, not homicide!
[gulps] Fine, the festival's my hunting ground. You've got me.
[licks lips] The river festival serves ME the finest catch.

barmaid.text: My river punch? [nervously] Extra strong. Keeps the festival crowd... wobbly.
A tipsy crowd near deep water? What could POSSIBLY go wrong. Heh.
The fisherman gone? Our festival plan drifts away with him.
I pour a strong drink! It's a FESTIVAL!
[gulps] Fine, the punch was meant to make you all... unsteady.
[licks lips] Drink up, the river's thirsty tonight.

mayor.text: The harvest moon festival is upon us. May it be safe. It won't be.
The farmer and baker host the harvest moon feast. Under a FULL moon.
With the farmer gone, the harvest moon feels less... hungry.
I'll shorten the festivities. Home before moonrise!
A harvest moon feeds more than the fields.

butcher.text: A feast under a FULL harvest moon? Whoever planned that is bold. Or a wolf.
The farmer's eyes glowed under the harvest moon. I saw it.
The farmer howled at the harvest moon! Not a toast, a CALL!
I'll carve the harvest roast with one eye on the sky.
Full moons and feasts don't mix.

baker.text: My harvest moon loaf? [nervously] Baked under moonlight. It brings out the... flavor.
The harvest moon makes me bake things I... can't quite remember.
The farmer gone? We harvested such fine ingredients together.
A baker loves a harvest! It's my busiest season!
[gulps] Fine, the moon does something to me. And my recipes.
[licks lips] Under the harvest moon, everything tastes richer.

blacksmith.text: I forged the harvest moon lanterns. The farmer wanted them dim. Very dim.
The farmer kept steering everyone away from the lanterns. Into the dark.
The farmer arranged the whole feast for moonrise. He's the wolf!
Claw marks on the harvest wagon this morning.
The farmer AND baker, feasting under a full moon? Doubly cursed!
The harvest moon shines on guilty faces.

beggar.text: I watched the harvest feast from the hedgerow. The moon made two of them... change.
The farmer and baker slipped into the fields as the moon rose.
Told you the moon brought out the beast! One caught!
There are hoof AND paw prints all through the harvest field.
Spare a coin under this hungry harvest moon!

farmer.text: The harvest moon and I go way back. [nervously] It's a... special night for me.
Something about the full moon over my fields just... awakens me.
The baker gone? We celebrated the harvest moon so well together.
A farmer celebrates the harvest! It's TRADITION!
[gulps] Fine, I don't just HARVEST under the moon.
[low growl] ...The harvest moon calls me to feed.

fisherman.text: The harvest moon lit the river red. Ominous festival, this one.
The baker's bread glowed strange under the harvest moon.
The baker's moon-loaf snarled when I bit it! Cursed harvest!
A harvest wreath floated down my river, torn to shreds.
I'll fish, not feast, under that moon.

barmaid.text: The harvest feast packed my inn, then emptied it into the moonlit fields.
The farmer and baker toasted to 'a moonlit harvest'. Creepy toast.
The farmer downed his cider then HOWLED at the moon. Clocked it!
Two of them worship that harvest moon far too much.
One moon-wolf caught! Happy harvest, indeed.
[sighs] I'm drawing the curtains next full moon.

mayor.text: The old tower is locked for public safety. Nothing to see. Move along!
The tower stays LOCKED by my order. Its contents are... classified.
The blacksmith gone? He made the only key to my tower. Pity.
A mayor secures dangerous structures! Stop prying!
[gulps] The tower holds evidence. Against me. That's why it's locked.
[clears throat] What's in the tower stays in the tower.

butcher.text: Why lock the old tower NOW, mid-crisis? What's the mayor hiding?
The mayor and blacksmith are the only two with tower keys. Suspicious.
The mayor locked the tower to hide his OWN evidence! Wolf!
I'll break that tower lock with my cleaver.
Locked doors hide the worst secrets.

baker.text: The mayor had me deliver bread to the tower. Then locked it behind me.
I heard scratching from inside the locked tower. Something's IN there.
Growling echoed down from the tower window.
The mayor AND blacksmith holding the only keys? They're hiding a den!
My bread went in. I'm glad I came out.

blacksmith.text: I forged the tower's lock. [nervously] And the only key. It's very... secure.
Only the mayor and I can open the tower. For good reason. Heh.
The mayor gone? He and I kept the tower's secret so well.
I make locks! That's my TRADE! It means nothing!
[low growl] Fine, the tower hides what the mayor and I did.
[low growl] ...The tower keeps our secret sealed tight.

beggar.text: I tried to shelter in the tower. It was locked AND occupied. Both!
The mayor and blacksmith unlock the tower at midnight, together.
Told you that tower hid a beast! One caught!
There are bones stacked at the base of the tower stairs.
Spare a coin for the locked-out witness!

farmer.text: The mayor locked the tower right after my sheep started vanishing.
I found paw prints leading to the tower's locked door.
Two figures with keys entered the tower at midnight.
One tower-wolf caught! Unlock it and let's see the truth.
You lock a tower to hide what howls inside.

fisherman.text: The tower overlooks my river. Its window glowed all night.
The mayor and blacksmith climbed the tower at dusk with a heavy sack.
The mayor watched the river from that tower, choosing targets!
A key washed down my river. A tower key, I'd wager.
Even a locked tower can't dam the river's truth.

barmaid.text: The mayor and blacksmith left my inn toward the locked tower. Nightly.
Those two whisper about 'the tower' over every pint.
The blacksmith bragged only HE could open the tower. Now I know why!
Two of them hold the only keys AND all the guilt.
One caught! The locked tower's secret is out.
[sighs] Whatever's in that tower can STAY there.

mayor.text: Snow blankets the village, yet strange tracks cut right through it.
The tracks in the snow lead from the beggar's spot to the river.
With the beggar gone, no fresh tracks in the snow. Curious.
Fresh snow keeps an honest record.
Winter hides nothing for long.

butcher.text: These snow tracks are too big for any villager's boots.
The fisherman's prints in the snow doubled back on themselves.
The fisherman's tracks led from the river to the bodies!
I'll follow those tracks with my cleaver.
Snow tells on the sneakiest of us.

baker.text: My bakery's snowed in. Perfect weather for staying suspicious.
Paw prints crossed my snowy doorstep at midnight.
I heard crunching snow and a howl before dawn.
Two sets of tracks in the snow? A pair of winter wolves!
My warm bread's the only comfort in this cold.

blacksmith.text: I forged snow cleats for the village. The beggar wanted a pair. Odd.
The beggar leaves tracks all over, then denies going out.
The beggar's snow tracks turned to PAW prints! He's the wolf!
Claw marks in the frost on my forge door.
Iron and ice both keep their secrets cold.

beggar.text: Tracks in the snow? [nervously] I have to walk SOMEWHERE to stay warm!
The snow covers my tracks by morning. Usually. Convenient.
The fisherman gone? We trudged through the snow together, he and I.
A beggar wanders! It's COLD! I'm just looking for warmth!
[gulps] Fine, those aren't boot prints in the snow.
[licks lips] Winter nights bring the loneliest, tastiest wanderers.

farmer.text: The snow killed my winter crop AND revealed monster tracks.
I followed the tracks from my barn to the frozen river.
Two trails in the snow met at the river's edge.
One snow-wolf caught! My frostbitten fields can rest.
Snow doesn't lie. People leave prints.

fisherman.text: My tracks by the river? [nervously] I ice-fish in winter! It's my LIVELIHOOD!
The frozen river's so quiet in winter. Perfect for... solitude. Heh.
The beggar gone? We shared the snowy riverbank on cold nights.
A fisherman works the winter river! Those are just my boots!
[gulps] Fine, I don't fish those tracks. I HUNT them.
[licks lips] The cold makes the catch keep longer.

barmaid.text: The whole village huddles in my inn. Except two who keep going OUT.
The fisherman and beggar left together, tracking snow behind them.
The fisherman left into the snow 'for fish' at MIDNIGHT. Sus!
Two of them brave the blizzard nightly. Why?!
One winter wolf caught! The snow gave them away.
[sighs] Stamp the snow off before you enter MY inn!

mayor.text: The midnight train is a triumph of my administration! It runs so... discreetly.
The train lets a man leave and return unseen. For BUSINESS, of course.
The butcher gone? He rode the midnight train with me so often.
A mayor builds infrastructure! The train is PROGRESS!
[gulps] The train's my escape route. After... certain nights.
[clears throat] All aboard the midnight train. Mind the... remains.

butcher.text: The midnight train? [nervously] I use it for meat deliveries. Late ones.
The train drops me far from the village. Nobody sees where I go. Heh.
The mayor gone? We rode the midnight train to our... hunting grounds.
A butcher ships MEAT by rail! It's efficient!
[gulps] Fine, the train's how I slip away after a kill.
[licks lips] The midnight train always brings me back hungry.

baker.text: The midnight train whistle wakes the whole village. Who rides at midnight?
The mayor and butcher are the only midnight passengers.
The mayor boards the train right after each attack. Escaping!
I heard howling from the departing train.
The mayor AND butcher on that train? A getaway for two wolves!
I bake at dawn, not board trains at midnight.

blacksmith.text: I forged the train's iron wheels. The mayor wanted them QUIET.
The butcher's midnight cargo clinks like bones on that train.
The butcher loaded 'meat crates' onto the train. They were DRIPPING.
Claw marks on the train carriage doors.
A quiet train is a suspicious train.

beggar.text: I ride the rails for free. That midnight train carries... passengers who don't return.
The mayor and butcher board every midnight, dragging heavy sacks.
Told you the train was a getaway! One wolf caught!
There are bones in the train's freight car. I've seen them!
Spare a coin for a stowaway witness!

farmer.text: The train tracks cut through my land. Something big rides at night.
Paw prints run alongside the tracks toward the station.
Two passengers boarded at midnight and returned before dawn.
One train-wolf caught! Derailed, permanently.
A midnight train carries more than freight.

fisherman.text: The train crosses my river bridge at midnight. Its cargo smells of blood.
The mayor and butcher watched the river from the train windows.
The mayor waved from the midnight train, escaping the scene!
A passenger's hat floated down my river from the bridge.
The river runs slower than that guilty train.

barmaid.text: The mayor and butcher leave my inn for the midnight train. Every night.
Those two check the train timetable like it's their alibi.
The butcher bragged the train 'takes him where the meat is'. EW!
Two of them ride that train to somewhere they won't name.
One caught! The midnight train's last stop is justice.
[sighs] My inn's the LAST stop before their little escape.

mayor.text: A treasure hunt for the village founding! Everyone's out digging. At night.
The blacksmith forged the treasure clues. The beggar hid them. Cozy.
With the blacksmith gone, the treasure maps stopped appearing. Odd.
I'll oversee this treasure hunt personally.
Some hunts dig up more than gold.

butcher.text: A midnight treasure hunt during a wolf crisis? Whose bright idea?
The blacksmith's clues sent hunters into the darkest corners.
The blacksmith's 'treasure map' led folks straight to the attacks!
I'll dig for treasure with my cleaver ready.
A treasure hunt's the perfect bait.

baker.text: I sold snacks to the treasure hunters. Nervous, spade-wielding crowd.
The beggar knew exactly where every clue led. Suspicious.
The beggar 'hid the treasure' where the hunters got picked off!
I heard growling from one of the dig sites.
The blacksmith AND beggar ran the hunt? They dug the TRAPS!
The only treasure I trust is fresh bread.

blacksmith.text: I forged the treasure clues. [nervously] They lead... interesting places. At night.
The hunt scatters everyone into the dark. Alone. Convenient for... reasons.
The beggar gone? He hid my clues so cleverly, he did.
I just made the CLUES! It's a fun game!
[low growl] Fine, the treasure map leads to ME.
[low growl] ...The real treasure is a village left alone in the dark.

beggar.text: I hid the treasure clues. [nervously] I know these hiding spots... intimately.
I sent hunters to the loneliest corners. For the... challenge. Heh.
The blacksmith gone? We planned the whole hunt together, he and I.
A beggar knows the village nooks! That's all!
[gulps] Fine, the treasure hunt was my hunting ground.
[licks lips] X marks the spot where dinner waits.

farmer.text: Treasure hunters trampled my fields all night. Found only paw prints.
The clues led hunters right past my haunted barn.
Two organizers slipped away while everyone dug.
One treasure-wolf caught! Keep the gold, I want my crops.
The only thing buried here is the truth.

fisherman.text: A treasure clue said 'seek by the river'. I found a torn shoe.
The blacksmith and beggar watched the hunters from the shadows.
The blacksmith's clues sent people to their doom, not gold!
A treasure map washed down my river, stained red.
The river's the only treasure I need.

barmaid.text: The treasure hunt emptied my inn into the dark. Bad for business, worse for survival.
The blacksmith and beggar toasted 'a successful hunt' before it started.
The beggar bragged he 'knows where the bodies— er, treasure is'. CLOCKED!
Two of them planned this hunt a little too carefully.
One caught! The lost treasure was a lost cause.
[sighs] The only treasure in MY inn is the ale.

mayor.text: The inn is said to be haunted now. Guests check in and never check out!
The barmaid runs that inn, the fisherman drinks there nightly. Cozy pair.
With the barmaid gone, the inn's 'hauntings' have ceased. Telling.
I'll have the inn investigated. Ghosts don't leave claw marks.
A haunted inn is often just a hungry one.

butcher.text: Guests vanish from that inn overnight. No ghost does THAT.
The barmaid always books the vanished guests into the back rooms.
The barmaid's rooms are where the guests DISAPPEAR! She's the wolf!
I'll bring my cleaver to that haunted inn.
The dead don't check out. The eaten do.

baker.text: I deliver bread to the inn. The 'haunted' rooms smell of blood.
The fisherman knows which guests are travelling alone. Always asks.
The fisherman lurks at the inn every night. Waiting for lone guests!
I heard howling from the inn's cellar.
The barmaid AND fisherman haunting that inn? A wolf lair!
My bread's the only thing that leaves that inn intact.

blacksmith.text: I fixed the inn's locks. The barmaid wanted them to lock from OUTSIDE.
The barmaid asked for locks only she controls. Chilling.
The barmaid locks guests IN, not out! Now the 'haunting' makes sense!
Claw marks on the inn's guest room doors.
No ghost needs a lock. A wolf does.

beggar.text: I beg outside the inn. Guests go in singing, and never come out!
The barmaid and fisherman whisper over the guest ledger nightly.
Told you that inn was deadly! One wolf caught!
There are travellers' bags piled in the inn cellar. Empty ones.
Spare a coin, but don't book a room!

farmer.text: My cousin stayed at the inn last week. Haven't seen him since.
Paw prints lead from the inn's back door to the woods.
Two staff slipped out the inn's cellar with heavy sacks.
One inn-wolf caught! May my cousin rest easy.
A haunted inn is a farmer's worst rumour.

fisherman.text: Me, at the inn? [nervously] I'm a REGULAR! I just... like the atmosphere.
I always know which guests travel alone. For friendly chats! Obviously.
The barmaid gone? We ran that inn's little secret so well.
A man can love his local inn! It's not a crime!
[gulps] Fine, I don't go to the inn to drink.
[licks lips] The inn's lone travellers make the finest company.

barmaid.text: My inn, haunted? [nervously] It's just... old floorboards. And, er, guests moving on.
A good innkeeper knows which guests won't be... missed. Heh.
The fisherman gone? Our little inn arrangement is finished.
My inn is cozy, not cursed! People love it here!
[gulps] Fine, the guests don't leave because I don't LET them.
[licks lips] Check-in's easy. It's the check-out that's tricky.

mayor.text: The crystal cave glitters with clues, and half of them lead to the forge.
The farmer guards the cave, the blacksmith's tools litter it. Why?
With the farmer gone, no one guards the crystal cave. Interesting.
I'll have that cave surveyed by torchlight.
Even crystal can't hide a dark deed.

butcher.text: Why are forge tools scattered in the crystal cave?
The blacksmith's hammer was found deep in the crystal cave.
The blacksmith's tools in the cave? It's his SECOND lair!
Cleaver's coming to that glittering deathtrap.
Pretty caves hide ugly truths.

baker.text: The crystal cave's beautiful, but it reeks of the forge and something worse.
I heard growling echo off the crystal walls.
Fur was snagged on the crystals near the entrance.
The farmer AND blacksmith in that cave? Their crystal den!
My bread stays out of caves, thank you.

blacksmith.text: My tools in the crystal cave? [nervously] I, uh, mine crystals. For decoration.
The cave's the perfect hideaway. Sparkly AND private. Heh.
The farmer gone? We shared that glittering cave, he and I.
A smith gathers materials! Crystals make fine inlays!
[low growl] Fine, the cave's my den. The crystals are just a bonus.
[low growl] ...The cave glitters like eyes in the dark.

beggar.text: I shelter in the crystal cave. Lately it's full of tools. And GROWLING.
The farmer and blacksmith slip into the crystal cave at midnight.
Told you that cave had a beast! One caught!
There's a nest of fur and forge-tools in the deepest crystal chamber.
Spare a coin for the cave-dwelling witness!

farmer.text: I guard the crystal cave. [nervously] For, um, the village's crystal reserves.
Nobody enters my cave but me. And my forge-loving friend. Heh.
The blacksmith gone? We kept the crystal cave so well together.
It's village property! A farmer protects it!
[gulps] Fine, I don't guard crystals. I guard our DEN.
[low growl] ...The cave's dark heart suits me fine.

fisherman.text: An underground stream from the cave feeds my river. It carried clues down.
The blacksmith and farmer vanished into that cave at dusk.
The blacksmith's cave tools washed into my river. His lair's exposed!
A crystal shard and a tuft of fur washed into my nets together.
The stream tells on the cave.

barmaid.text: The farmer and blacksmith drink together, whispering about a 'crystal den'.
Those two leave for the cave the second I close up.
The farmer bragged the cave 'hides everything'. NOW I listen!
Two of them share a glittering secret. And a guilty one.
One cave-wolf caught! The crystal den's exposed.
[sighs] A cave over my WARM inn? Suspicious taste.

mayor.text: The red moon rises tonight. A rare omen! I've, ah, cleared my schedule.
The red moon is just a natural wonder! Everyone stay in. Except me.
The baker gone? We so enjoyed the red moon together, he and I.
A mayor observes celestial events! It's SCIENCE!
[gulps] The red moon does something to me. And to my... appetite.
[clears throat] Bask in the red moon, villagers. While you can.

butcher.text: Under the red moon, everyone's uneasy. And two of them are TOO calm.
The mayor and baker watched the red moon rise, grinning.
The mayor welcomed the red moon like an old friend! He's a wolf!
I'll carve by red moonlight, cleaver in hand.
A red moon reddens more than the sky.

baker.text: The red moon? [nervously] I bake special crimson loaves for the occasion.
The red moon makes my bread come out the loveliest shade of... blood.
The mayor gone? We watched the red moon rise together, he and I.
A themed loaf! The red moon inspires me artistically!
[gulps] Fine, the red moon brings out my true nature. And my recipes.
[licks lips] Red moon, red bread, red everything. Delicious.

blacksmith.text: I forged red-moon charms for the villagers. The mayor bought a dozen.
The baker and mayor stood together, bathing in the red light.
The baker's crimson bread under a red moon? He's the beast!
Claw marks glinted red in the moonlight on my forge.
The mayor AND baker allied under the red moon? A blood pact!
A red moon reveals red hands.

beggar.text: Under the red moon, I watched the mayor and baker... change. I SWEAR.
The baker and mayor met beneath the red moon, whispering.
Told you the red moon unmasks them! One caught!
There are red-tinged paw prints all down the main street.
Spare a coin under this bloody moon!

farmer.text: The red moon drove my animals into a frenzy. They sense the blood.
Paw prints, red as the moon, circle my farmhouse.
Two figures crossed the fields under the crimson light.
One red-moon wolf caught! My herd can breathe again.
A red moon never bodes well for a farmer.

fisherman.text: The red moon turned my river to blood. Fittingly grim.
The baker's crimson loaf drifted down my river under the red moon.
The mayor stood on the bank, drinking in the red moon. Wolfishly!
Something red-furred slipped along the bank in the crimson light.
The river reflects the moon's guilt.

barmaid.text: The red moon packed my inn with frightened villagers. Except two, who left.
The baker and mayor slipped out the moment the red moon rose.
The baker toasted the red moon with a CRIMSON drink. Clocked it!
Two of them love that bloody moon far too much.
One caught! The red moon spilled their secret.
[sighs] I'm boarding my windows next red moon.

mayor.text: A travelling circus arrived. The whole village is dazzled. Perhaps too dazzled.
The butcher supplies the circus meat, the barmaid the drinks. Cozy.
With the butcher gone, the circus lost its... backstage helper. Hmm.
I'll keep a close eye on this circus.
A circus is all misdirection. Perfect for a wolf.

butcher.text: The circus? [nervously] I just supply the... animal feed. Very fresh feed.
Everyone's watching the trapeze, nobody's watching me. Convenient. Heh.
The barmaid gone? She kept the crowd cheering while I... worked.
A butcher feeds the circus beasts! It's a JOB!
[gulps] Fine, I use the circus crowds as cover.
[licks lips] The circus crowd is packed shoulder to... snack.

baker.text: I sold pastries at the circus. Grand show, until a spectator vanished.
The barmaid served drinks that kept everyone staring at the ring.
The barmaid's circus punch had the crowd too giddy to notice the screams!
Under the circus music, I heard a growl from the tents.
The butcher AND barmaid working the circus? A two-wolf act!
My pastries were the only honest act in town.

blacksmith.text: I forged the circus cages. The butcher asked for EXTRA strong bars.
The butcher's circus 'feed' barrels dripped something red.
The butcher wanted cages 'to keep things IN'. Himself, maybe!
Claw marks on the circus tent poles.
The greatest show hides the greatest lies.

beggar.text: The circus let me in free! Then a clown vanished mid-act. Poof!
The butcher and barmaid slip behind the tents between every act.
Told you the circus was a cover! One wolf caught!
There's a pile of torn circus costumes behind the big top.
Spare a coin for the front-row witness!

farmer.text: The circus 'borrowed' my animals. Fewer came back than left.
Paw prints circle the circus tents at night.
Two performers hauled heavy trunks out after closing.
One circus-wolf caught! The show's finally over.
A circus is a farmer's missing-livestock nightmare.

fisherman.text: The circus set up by my river. Odd splashing behind the tents at night.
The butcher and barmaid whispered behind the big top nightly.
The butcher dumped 'circus scraps' in my river. They had FINGERS!
A spangled costume floated down my river, torn to shreds.
The river's no part of their circus.

barmaid.text: My circus punch? [nervously] Extra festive! Keeps the crowd... distracted.
A dazzled, tipsy crowd notices nothing. Perfect for... the butcher. Heh.
The butcher gone? Our circus act loses its other half.
I pour drinks at events! It's a CIRCUS! People celebrate!
[gulps] Fine, the distraction was the whole point.
[licks lips] Roll up, roll up! Don't mind the missing acts.

mayor.text: A secret tunnel was found, running from the river straight to the forge.
The tunnel links the fisherman's river to the blacksmith's forge. Why?
With the fisherman gone, the tunnel's gone silent. Telling.
I'll have that tunnel sealed and searched.
Secret tunnels lead to secret crimes.

butcher.text: Who digs a tunnel from a river to a forge? What are they moving?
The fisherman's boots were muddy with forge-ash. From the tunnel!
The fisherman uses the tunnel to reach the forge unseen!
I'll take my cleaver down that tunnel.
Tunnels are for those with something to hide.

baker.text: The tunnel runs right under my bakery! I felt the digging for weeks.
Something big moves through that tunnel at night. I hear it.
Growling echoed up through my bakery floor from the tunnel.
The fisherman AND blacksmith share the tunnel? Their secret highway!
My cellar's cracked from all their digging.

blacksmith.text: A tunnel from my forge? [nervously] For, um, ventilation. Long-distance ventilation.
The tunnel lets me move about unseen. Very handy for... late errands. Heh.
The fisherman gone? We used that tunnel together, he and I.
A forge needs airflow! It's engineering!
[low growl] Fine, the tunnel's how the fisherman and I stay hidden.
[low growl] ...The tunnel's dark is where I feel most at home.

beggar.text: I shelter in that tunnel. It runs from the river to the forge. And it GROWLS.
The fisherman and blacksmith slip through the tunnel every midnight.
Told you the tunnel had a beast! One caught!
There are bones lining the tunnel walls, river to forge.
Spare a coin for the tunnel-dwelling witness!

farmer.text: The tunnel collapsed part of my field! What are they digging for?
Paw prints lead from the tunnel mouth to my paddock.
Two figures vanished into the tunnel, dragging sacks.
One tunnel-wolf caught! Fill that hole in already.
You dig a secret tunnel to hide a secret hunger.

fisherman.text: The tunnel from my river? [nervously] I, uh, dug it for... irrigation. Forge irrigation.
The tunnel lets me reach the forge without a soul seeing. Handy. Heh.
The blacksmith gone? We built that tunnel together, he and I.
A fisherman manages water! Tunnels move water!
[gulps] Fine, the tunnel's how I move my... catch unseen.
[licks lips] The tunnel carries my catch straight to the den.

barmaid.text: The fisherman and blacksmith leave my inn and just... vanish underground.
Those two whisper about a tunnel between river and forge.
The fisherman bragged about his 'secret shortcut'. NOW I get it!
Two of them share an underground secret. And a guilty look.
One caught! The secret tunnel's exposed.
[sighs] Use the DOOR like normal people!

mayor.text: Tonight I crown the village's honorary king! A golden crown, a grand ceremony.
The whole village gathers for the crowning. At night. How... convenient.
The beggar gone? He helped me plan the ceremony from the shadows.
A mayor honours tradition with pomp! Nothing more!
[gulps] The ceremony's a cover. For me. You've nearly got it.
[clears throat] Long live the king! And the... crowd. For now.

butcher.text: A grand crown ceremony while villagers vanish? The mayor's distracting us.
The mayor and beggar planned this ceremony together. Odd pairing.
The mayor staged the ceremony to hide his own crimes! Wolf!
I'll attend the crowning with my cleaver.
A crown can't hide a bloody hand.

baker.text: I baked the ceremonial cake, shaped like a golden crown.
The beggar lurked at the ceremony, whispering to the mayor.
The beggar 'helping' with the ceremony? He knew who'd slip away!
Under the fanfare, I heard howling from the square.
The mayor AND beggar behind the ceremony? A royal conspiracy!
My crown cake outshone the real one, if I say so.

blacksmith.text: I forged the golden crown itself. The mayor wanted it HEAVY.
The mayor arranged the ceremony for the darkest night. Suspicious.
The mayor kept the crowd bowing while he slipped away. Wolf trick!
Claw marks on the ceremonial dais this morning.
Gold crowns, guilty heads.

beggar.text: Me, at the crowning? [nervously] I just... watch from the crowd. Always watching.
A big ceremony means everyone's looking one way. I look the OTHER way. Heh.
The mayor gone? We planned the ceremony together, he and I.
A beggar attends free events! Is that a crime?!
[gulps] Fine, I helped stage the ceremony. As cover.
[licks lips] All hail the king. And pass the... refreshments.

farmer.text: The whole village at the crowning means my farm's wide open tonight.
Paw prints lead from the ceremony square to my fields.
The mayor and beggar left the ceremony at the same moment.
One crowned wolf caught! Some ceremony THIS was.
A crowd bowing to a crown is a beast's easy feast.

fisherman.text: The crown ceremony lit up the whole riverside. Grand, until the screaming.
The mayor and beggar whispered by the river before the ceremony.
The mayor waved the crown then vanished toward the dark. Sus!
A ceremonial sash floated down my river, torn.
No crown rules the river.

barmaid.text: The crowning packed my inn, then emptied it into the square.
The mayor and beggar toasted to 'a memorable ceremony'. Chilling.
The beggar let slip he 'knows who won't see the crowning end'. CLOCKED!
Two of them staged this ceremony a little too eagerly.
One caught! The golden crown's deception is exposed.
[sighs] A crown ceremony at MIDNIGHT? Read the room, mayor.

mayor.text: The final festival of the season is tonight. May we all survive it.
The farmer runs the festival games, the barmaid the bar. Cozy pair.
With the farmer gone, the final festival feels safer already.
I'll cut the festival short at the first howl.
A final festival can be someone's last.

butcher.text: The final festival gathers everyone in the fields at dusk. Reckless.
The farmer set the festival in the darkest corner of his land.
The farmer lured us all to HIS fields for the finale. It's a hunt!
I'll bring my cleaver to the festival finale.
The last festival is the deadliest.

baker.text: I baked the festival's farewell feast. Beautiful night, until the screams.
The barmaid served a farewell drink that left folk dizzy.
The barmaid's farewell punch had everyone stumbling in the dark fields!
Between the fireworks, I heard howling across the fields.
The farmer AND barmaid ran the final festival? A closing-night hunt!
My farewell loaves were the safest thing there.

blacksmith.text: I forged the festival's finale lanterns. The farmer wanted them DIM.
The farmer marked the festival paths with strange dark flags.
The farmer steered everyone away from the light. Into HIS jaws!
Claw marks on the festival stage this morning.
The final festival lit only guilty faces.

beggar.text: The final festival let me in! Then guests started dropping into the dark.
The farmer and barmaid signaled each other across the fields.
Told you the finale was a trap! One wolf caught!
There are torn festival banners piled behind the barn.
Spare a coin at the final festival!

farmer.text: My final festival! [nervously] Everyone gathers on MY land. How... fitting.
I know every dark corner of these fields. Perfect for a grand... finale. Heh.
The barmaid gone? We ran the finale together, she and I.
I HOST the festival on my land! That's generosity!
[gulps] Fine, the festival's my final hunting ground.
[low growl] ...The final festival feeds me best of all.

fisherman.text: The final festival spilled onto my riverbank. Odd splashing at midnight.
The barmaid and farmer whispered by the river before the finale.
The barmaid's punch had folk staggering toward the deep water!
A festival garland floated down my river, shredded.
The river hosts no final hunt.

barmaid.text: My farewell punch? [nervously] Extra special. For a MEMORABLE final festival.
A tipsy crowd on a dark farm? A recipe for a great... closing act. Heh.
The farmer gone? Our grand finale falls apart without him.
I pour a festive drink! It's the FINALE!
[gulps] Fine, the punch was meant to make you all... easy.
[licks lips] Last festival, last call, last... everything.

mayor.text: It's the last midnight of the moon cycle. The final clues point to two shops.
Both the bakery and the butcher shop hide the final evidence.
With the baker gone, the bakery's dark and the clues run cold.
Tonight we end this. Search both shops!
The last midnight always tells the truth.

butcher.text: Clues in MY shop? [nervously] Just... the usual butcher business. Very usual.
The bakery and my shop share more than a wall. And a secret. Heh.
The baker gone? We hid our secret so well between our two shops.
A butcher's shop is full of MEAT! What did you expect?!
[gulps] Fine, the final clue's behind my counter. You've got me.
[licks lips] The last midnight, the freshest cut.

baker.text: The final clues, in MY bakery? [nervously] It's flour and yeast, I swear!
The bakery and butcher shop have a little... connecting secret. Heh.
The butcher gone? We shared everything between our shops. Even the... evidence.
A bakery hides only BREAD! Leave my ovens alone!
[gulps] Fine, the last clue's baked into my biggest loaf.
[licks lips] On the last midnight, I bake my finest yet.

blacksmith.text: I forged a hidden door between the bakery and the butcher shop. They INSISTED.
The butcher's cleaver came back stained too often. Now, on the last night...
The butcher and baker share a secret door! Two wolves, one lair!
Claw marks on both shop doors this last midnight.
The baker AND butcher, connected shops, final clues? Case closed!
Two shops, one secret, one last night.

beggar.text: On the last midnight, I saw the baker and butcher pass a sack between shops.
The baker and butcher meet through a hidden door at midnight.
Told you those two shops were linked! One wolf caught!
There are final clues in both shops. Bones and bread, side by side.
Spare a coin on this last midnight!

farmer.text: On the last night, the butcher's shop overflows with meat I never sold him.
My final missing sheep led right to the space between the two shops.
Two figures moved between the shops, dragging the final sacks.
One caught on the last midnight! Justice, at last.
The last midnight settles every count.

fisherman.text: On the last midnight, a bloody parcel washed from the shops into my river.
The baker and butcher whispered through their shared wall all night.
The baker's final loaf snarled when I cut it! The last clue confirmed!
The river gave up the last clue: a torn apron, baker's and butcher's both.
On the last midnight, the river tells all.

barmaid.text: On this last midnight, the baker and butcher left my inn together. Grinning.
Those two toast to their 'connected shops' every single night.
The butcher bragged his shop 'holds the final secret'. CLOCKED, on the last night!
Two of them share a wall AND all the guilt.
One caught on the last midnight! The mystery's finally solved.
[sighs] Last midnight, last order, last chance. Choose wisely.

mayor.text: The old well ran dry overnight, then filled with something dark by dawn. Unnatural.
I've forbidden villagers from the well after dark. For everyone's safety.
A well that empties and refills itself? Someone is tampering with it.
Order will be restored, one bucket at a time.

butcher.text: Two shadows lower something heavy into that well every midnight. I've watched them.
The water came back up red. I know red when I see it.
I keep my cleaver close whenever I pass that well now.
A well should give water, not swallow villagers.

baker.text: I drew water from the well and it smelled of wet fur, not stone.
My dough wouldn't rise with water from that cursed well.
Something splashed down there when no one had thrown anything in.
I'll fetch my water from the stream from now on, thank you.

blacksmith.text: I forged a new bucket chain for the well. The farmer wanted it EXTRA long.
Claw marks scored the well's stone rim this morning.
Iron doesn't lie: something with claws climbs out of that shaft.
A well that deep hides far more than water.

beggar.text: I sleep by the well for shelter. Last night it GROWLED at me.
I saw the fisherman and farmer haul a dripping sack to the well's edge.
There's a nest of bones wedged in the old well bucket.
Spare a coin for the well's only witness!

farmer.text: Me, at the well? [nervously] I just... water my crops. Late. Very late.
A farmer needs water! That's ALL I fetch from that well!
[low growl] ...The bottom of that well is so pleasantly dark.
[licks lips] The well always sends up the freshest catch.

fisherman.text: The well connects to my river underground. [nervously] So of course I check it.
Howling from the well? Must be the wind down the shaft. Definitely the wind.
[licks lips] The well water tastes so much better after midnight.
A fisherman knows every dark, deep place. The well included.

barmaid.text: My patrons won't draw water after dark now. Bad for the inn.
The fisherman and farmer left my inn heading for the well. Together. Again.
Something down that well hums when the moon is full.
[sighs] I'm serving cider until that well behaves.

casualWait: You decide to chill out a bit.
You hang around a bit instead.
You hang tight for a moment.
